record.note: Prompts and model reasoning are not stored, so they are not here. Each call lists the tokens the model spent reasoning.

attempt.objective: A full game with no human player, played to Fall 1999 or a solo win.

messages.body: Austria here. I'm not planning to move on Venice or Trieste-adjacent Italian holdings this turn. Could you confirm you won't attack Trieste? I'd rather we both push against Russia and Turkey, leaving each other's home centers alone.

Austria to Russia: I have no quarrel with you this spring. My armies in Bohemia and Galicia are aimed at the south. If you keep Warsaw and Galicia unthreatened by your own moves, I'll keep my forces away from Galicia. Are you planning anything against me?

Austria to Turkey: I'm concerned about Serbia and Rumania, which are both open. I propose we each take one: I take Serbia, you take Rumania and Bulgaria. Neither of us needs to fight the other while Russia is strong. Let me know your intentions.

I propose a clear Channel understanding: I’ll keep F LON out of ENG this spring if F BRE stays out of ENG. I’m aiming F EDI-NWG and F LON-NTH, with Norway as my autumn objective. What are your plans for the Channel and Belgium?

I’m aiming to take Norway and would like a quiet North Sea. I propose F LON-NTH and F EDI-NWG; please keep F KIE out of NTH. Are you planning KIE-DEN, and would you be open to coordinating over Belgium and Holland?

I intend to move F EDI-NWG and seek Norway in autumn. Could we agree not to contest Norway this year? You could use F STP/South toward BOT; let me know your plans for Finland and the northern centers.

France here. Let's keep the Channel quiet this spring. I'll move my fleet away from the Channel and won't threaten London or Edinburgh. Are you planning anything against Belgium or Holland? I'd rather we both expand elsewhere.

France to Germany: I have no interest in attacking you. Could you tell me your plans for Belgium and Burgundy? If you stay out of Paris's neighborhood, I can focus my armies on Spain and Italy, away from your borders.

France to Italy: Marseille and Piedmont are sensitive for both of us. I propose we both leave each other alone this year. I will hold Marseille and not move toward Piedmont. Would you consider taking Tunis and staying south while I take Spain?

Let’s keep Burgundy demilitarized this spring: I’ll keep my army out of Burgundy, and ask that A Paris stays out of Burgundy. We can both focus on neutral centers rather than opening a fight immediately.
I intend to secure Denmark and Holland. Could you keep F Edinburgh out of the North Sea this spring and focus on Norway? I’ll avoid interfering with your Norwegian move.
Let’s avoid an early Baltic confrontation. Please keep F St. Petersburg (South) out of the Baltic this spring; I’ll keep my forces from moving against Russia. What are your plans for Sweden?

Italy here. I have no interest in attacking you. Let's both keep our borders quiet: I'll hold Venice and Rome-area units defensively while you deal with Russia. Would you confirm you won't move on Venice or Trieste in 1901?

Italy to Turkey: I suggest we stay out of each other's way in the Eastern Mediterranean. Keep your fleets away from Ionian waters and I'll keep mine off Greece and Albania. Can you confirm your intentions toward Greece and Rome?

Italy to France: Tunis and Piedmont-area moves could sour things between us. I propose we both focus elsewhere this spring: you on Burgundy and Spain, me on Tunis and the Adriatic. Are you willing to stay out of Piedmont and Venice?
I intend to move toward Sweden. If you are aiming for Norway, let’s keep our northern openings clear of each other: I’ll avoid the Norwegian route, and ask that you leave Sweden to me.
I’m looking to secure Sweden this year. I propose we avoid conflict in the Baltic: I’ll keep my fleet out of the Baltic Sea, and ask that you leave Sweden uncontested.
Let’s keep the Black Sea clear this spring. I propose neither of us moves a fleet there; I’ll avoid the Black Sea if you do the same. What are your plans for Bulgaria and Rumania?

Turkey here. Russia is my main threat in the north. Would you consider keeping your armies out of Serbia and Greece this spring, and we can both focus on Russia and Italy? I will not move into Bulgaria against you if you leave Rumania alone too.

Turkey here. I have no quarrel with you if you stay out of the Black Sea and leave Armenia and Sevastopol alone. Your fleet in Sevastopol is an open invitation for me. Would you commit to Rumania and Galicia instead, away from my coast?

Austria here. Agreed, let's keep the peace. I won't move on Venice or Rome this spring. I expect you to leave Trieste alone; my fleet there stays put. Let's both look east and south toward Russia and Turkey.

Austria here. I'm willing to keep my armies out of Greece this spring. Serbia is different: I intend to take it, so I can't promise to stay out of there. If you leave Rumania and Bulgaria to your own efforts and don't push into Galicia or Bohemia, we need not fight each other while Russia is the bigger problem.

Agreed: I’ll keep F LON out of ENG, and ask that F BRE stay out as well. I plan F EDI-NWG and F LON-NTH, with Norway my autumn target. I’ll leave Belgium alone this spring; what is your intended move for F BRE?
I’ll keep F EDI out of NTH and move it to NWG; F LON-NTH is essential for Norway. Please keep F KIE out of NTH as proposed. I expect KIE-DEN is sensible; I’m not committing on Belgium or Holland yet.
Agreed: I’ll pursue Norway and leave Sweden to you. I plan F EDI-NWG and F LON-NTH; your avoiding the Norwegian route will keep things clear. Please let me know whether F STP/South is moving to BOT.

France to Italy: I can agree to stay out of Piedmont and Venice this spring. I will not move toward Piedmont. I'm going for Spain and Burgundy-area neutrals, so Tunis is yours to take if you want it, but please keep your fleets out of Western Mediterranean waters near Marseille.

France to Germany: Agreed, I will keep my army out of Burgundy this spring and my Paris army will not enter it. I'm focusing on Spain and the Western Mediterranean. Please keep your forces out of Belgium-adjacent moves against me, and tell me if you plan to take Holland or Belgium.

France to England: Agreed on the Channel. F BRE will stay out of ENG this spring, and I will not threaten London or Edinburgh. I'm not targeting Belgium or Holland this turn. Let's both take neutrals: you Norway, me Spain. Keep your fleets out of Brest's reach.
I’ll keep A Munich out of Burgundy this spring, as agreed. I do intend to pursue Belgium, so please keep A Paris out of Belgium; I’ll stay clear of your Spanish plans and avoid moves toward Paris.

Agreed: I’ll keep F Kiel out of the North Sea, and won’t interfere with your move toward Norway. I’m planning F Kiel-Denmark and A Munich-Ruhr, with Holland as a priority. Let’s leave Belgium open for now and avoid a clash there.
Agreed, I’ll keep my forces out of Russia and leave Sweden uncontested this spring. Please keep F St. Petersburg (South) out of the Baltic, as you propose; I’m planning F Kiel-Denmark.

Italy to France: Agreed in principle. I will not move toward Marseille or Piedmont this spring. My fleet and army will focus on Tunis and the Adriatic. Please keep your fleets out of the Western Mediterranean approaches to Naples and Rome, and we can talk again in autumn.

Italy to Austria: I confirm I will not attack Trieste or Venice this spring. My units will hold defensively and I am focused on the south and Adriatic. Please keep your forces away from Venice and Rome in 1901, and let us both gain ground against Russia and Turkey.
I have no plans against Austria. I’ll keep Warsaw and Galicia unthreatened this spring; my attention is on the northern centers and Rumania. I hope your forces stay clear of Galicia as proposed.

I’ll keep my fleet out of the Black Sea and won’t move against Armenia. I’m planning to send F Sevastopol to Rumania, not toward your coast. I can’t promise to leave Sevastopol alone in future, but I see no reason for conflict this spring.
Agreed: F St. Petersburg (South) will stay out of the Baltic this spring. I’m moving toward Sweden and ask that you leave it uncontested; I’ll avoid any move against Germany.
I’ll keep to our understanding: I’m aiming for Sweden, not Norway, and will avoid the Norwegian route. Please leave Sweden uncontested while you pursue Norway.

Turkey here. My fleet in Ankara and armies in Constantinople and Smyrna are aimed at Russia and the Black Sea for now. I have no plans for Greece or Rome this spring. Keep your fleets out of the Aegean and we will get along.

Turkey here. I still prefer we avoid each other while Russia is strong. I cannot promise to stay out of Rumania or Bulgaria, since Russia is my real concern. Keep Serbia and Greece quiet this spring and we can talk about Rumania later.

Turkey here. Agreed on the Black Sea this spring, provided your Sevastopol fleet stays put and does not move south or into Armenia. I will hold my fleets off the Black Sea as well. Let us talk again in the autumn.

Austria to Russia: Fall 1901. Rumania is contested between us, and Russian F RUM sits next to my Serbia push. I'd rather not fight you. Will you keep A UKR and F RUM out of Galicia and Bohemia, and tell me if you plan to move on Rumania or Bulgaria?
I’ll take Norway with F NTH supported by F NWG. Please keep F FIN off Norway as agreed and pursue Sweden; let me know if you see any risk to that plan.
I plan F NTH-Norway with support from F NWG. Please keep F DEN out of the North Sea and avoid Norway. I won’t contest your Holland or Denmark plans; can we leave Belgium open for now?
I’ll maintain our Channel understanding and keep F NTH and F NWG away from the Channel. I’m taking Norway; please confirm F MAO won’t move against ENG or the Irish Sea this turn.

France to Germany: Fall 1901. I hold Paris and Spain's approach, and I'm not moving toward Burgundy or Belgium. Are you still going after Belgium with your armies? I'd like your word that Munich and Ruhr stay out of Burgundy and Picardy while I work on Spain and Portugal.

France to England: Thanks for the Channel calm. My fleet in MAO is headed for Spain's coast, not the Channel. Are you taking Norway and Sweden this autumn? If so, I'll respect your North Sea moves and ask that your fleets stay out of the Bay of Biscay and Portugal.

France to Italy: Tunis is yours as agreed, and I'm not sending fleets into the Western Med near Naples or Rome. My army in Spain is for Spain and Portugal only. Please keep your fleets out of Marseille's approaches, and let's both avoid Piedmont this autumn.
I have F Denmark and A Ruhr this fall. I plan to secure Holland; please keep F North Sea out of Holland and Belgium so we avoid a clash. Are you still pursuing Norway with F Norwegian Sea?
I intend to move A Ruhr to Holland this fall and keep A Munich out of Burgundy. Are you planning to contest Belgium, or will you leave it open? I’ll stay clear of your Spanish position.
I’m keeping my forces out of Russia and the Baltic this fall. Is your fleet in Sweden, and do you still intend to avoid the Baltic?

Italy to Turkey: Fall 1901. I plan to move my ION fleet and ROM/VEN armies toward Tunis and the Adriatic, not Greece. Are you still set on Russia via Rumania and Bulgaria? If you take Greece later, I'd like your word it stays a one-time move, not a push on Naples.

My F RUM is holding the center this autumn, supported by A UKR if needed. Please keep A BUL and F ANK away from Rumania and the Black Sea; I’ll likewise avoid moves against your territory this turn. Can we renew our non-aggression understanding?
I’m moving F FIN to Sweden this autumn under our agreement. Please keep F DEN from moving to Sweden or supporting a contest there; I’ll keep my forces out of the Baltic and away from Germany.
I’m proceeding F FIN-SWE as agreed. Please leave Sweden uncontested while you take Norway; I’ll keep clear of the Norwegian route.

Turkey here. Your F Rumania sits next to my Bulgaria and Constantinople. Russia, I need to know: will F Rumania and A Ukraine stay out of Bulgaria and the Black Sea this autumn? I can keep A Bulgaria off Rumania if you give me the same assurance. Please answer before we move.
Confirmed: F MAO can stay out of ENG and the Irish Sea, and I’ll keep F NTH and F NWG away from the Channel. I’m taking Norway with F NTH supported by F NWG; I’m not pursuing Sweden.
Agreed. I’m taking Norway with F NTH supported by F NWG and will leave Sweden to F FIN. I see no risk to your move from my units.
Yes, I’m pursuing Norway with F NTH supported by F NWG. I’ll keep F NTH out of Holland and Belgium this turn; please keep F DEN clear of the North Sea as agreed.

France to England: Confirmed, F MAO is headed for Spain's coast and will not move against ENG or the Irish Sea. Good luck taking Norway. I ask that your fleets stay out of the Bay of Biscay and Portugal, and that F NTH and F NWG keep away from Brest's waters. Let's keep the Channel quiet.

France to Germany: I hear you plan A Ruhr to Holland. That is your business, and I will not contest Holland or Belgium this fall. My army in Paris stays out of Burgundy and Picardy for now. Please keep A Munich and A Ruhr away from Burgundy and Picardy, and I will keep my forces off your western centers.

Yes: A Ruhr-Holland, and I’ll keep A Munich out of Burgundy and Picardy. I’m not committing to Belgium this autumn; please keep Paris out of Belgium and leave it open while we take separate centers. Let me know if your plans change.

I’ll keep F Denmark out of the North Sea and Norway, and A Ruhr is going to Holland. Please keep F North Sea out of Holland and Belgium as proposed. Your Norway move is no concern to me; we can leave Belgium open this autumn.

I’m keeping F Denmark out of Sweden and the Baltic, and won’t support a contest there. I understand you’re moving F Finland to Sweden; I’ll stay clear of your position and continue to avoid moves against Russia.

Italy to France: Thanks for confirming. Tunis is my target this autumn, and I will keep my fleets out of Marseille's approaches and away from Piedmont. Please keep your Spain army in Iberia and out of the Western Med near Naples. If you move against Portugal or Spain only, we stay on good terms.

I’ll keep A UKR and F RUM out of Galicia and Bohemia. F RUM is holding the center this autumn; I have no move planned against Bulgaria. I’d prefer we avoid a contest over Rumania and keep our forces clear of each other.

Yes: F RUM and A UKR will stay out of Bulgaria and the Black Sea this autumn. F RUM will hold Rumania, with A UKR available to support it. Please keep A BUL and F ANK away from Rumania and the Black Sea as agreed.

I see no risk to our plan: I’m moving F FIN to Sweden and will keep clear of the Norwegian route. Germany has told me its forces will stay out of the Baltic and leave Sweden uncontested. Good luck taking Norway.

Yes, F FIN is moving to Sweden this autumn. I’ll continue to keep my forces out of the Baltic and away from Germany. Thanks for leaving Sweden uncontested; I trust F DEN will stay clear of any contest there.

Turkey here. Fall 1901: I have no orders toward Greece or Rome this autumn. My fleet stays in the eastern Aegean and my armies face Russia. I cannot promise a permanent arrangement, but I will not push on Naples this turn. Keep your ION fleet out of the Aegean and we are fine.

Austria to Turkey: Spring 1902. I'm taking Serbia this turn with my armies. Rumania is open; I won't contest it while Russia holds Sevastopol-area units. Will you keep A BUL and A CON away from Serbia and Greece? I'd like to hear your plans against Russia in the Black Sea.
I’m looking to expand into Belgium this year. Will you leave Belgium open and avoid moving F DEN or A HOL there? I’ll keep my forces out of Holland and Denmark; let me know your plans for Belgium.

Are you planning to move against Belgium or the Channel this spring? I’d like to take Belgium and can keep my fleets away from ENG and Brest if you’ll leave Belgium uncontested and maintain our Channel understanding.
Let’s keep our northern centers clear of conflict: I’ll avoid Sweden, and ask you not to contest Norway. What are your plans for F SWE and F STP this year?

France to Italy: Spring 1902. I'm keeping my army in Spain and Portugal and my fleets out of the Western Med near Naples and Rome. Are you still taking Tunis and holding Venice? I'd like confirmation that your forces stay out of Marseille and Piedmont this spring.

France to Germany: Spring 1902. My Paris army stays out of Burgundy and Picardy. Are you moving A Holland and A Munich as agreed, and is Belgium still open? I'd like your word that Ruhr and Munich stay out of Burgundy and Picardy while I take Spain and Portugal.

France to England: Spring 1902. F MAO stays out of the Irish Sea and ENG and is headed for Spain. Please keep your North Sea fleets out of the Channel and away from Brest. Good luck with Norway. Tell me if you plan any move toward Belgium or the Bay of Biscay.
I plan to take Belgium this spring with A Holland. Please keep A Paris out of Belgium and Burgundy; I’ll keep A Munich out of Burgundy and Picardy, and we can avoid an unnecessary western clash.

I intend to move A Holland to Belgium. Please keep any units out of Belgium this spring; I’ll keep F Denmark clear of the North Sea and your Norwegian position. Let me know if you have other plans for Belgium.

Let’s continue avoiding an early Baltic conflict. I have F Denmark and will keep it out of the Baltic and Sweden. Please keep F Sweden out of the Baltic this spring; are you planning to hold Sweden or move elsewhere?

Italy to Russia: Your fleets and armies are pressing Austria and Turkey. I have no quarrel with you. Will you keep Austria's east under pressure rather than moving into Rumania-Bulgaria against me? I'd like to know your Spring plans for Sweden and Warsaw before I commit my Adriatic fleet elsewhere.

I propose we renew our non-aggression pact: F Rumania holds, A Ukraine stays out of Galicia, and neither of us enters the Black Sea this spring. Please keep A Bulgaria and F Ankara away from Rumania; I’ll avoid Bulgaria and your territory.

I have no move planned against Austria. I’ll keep A Ukraine out of Galicia and F Rumania in place; please keep your forces out of Galicia and avoid any attack on Rumania. Can we keep the frontier quiet this spring?

I intend to keep clear of the Baltic and Germany this spring. Please keep F Denmark from contesting Sweden or moving against my fleet there; I’m not seeking a Baltic confrontation. What are your plans for Denmark and the Baltic?

Turkey here. Spring 1902: Russia's F RUM and A UKR are sitting next to my A BUL and A CON. I'm holding Bulgaria and Constantinople this spring. Will you confirm F RUM stays out of Bulgaria and Black Sea, and A UKR does not move to Sevastopol or Armenia? Then I'll keep my fleets off your coast.

Austria to Russia: Agreed on keeping the frontier quiet this spring. My armies are moving south into Serbia, not toward Galicia. I'm not planning any move against Rumania. Please keep A Ukraine and F Rumania out of Galicia and Bohemia, and let's both watch Turkey in the Black Sea. Tell me if your plans change.

I don’t plan to move against Belgium this spring, and I’ll keep my fleets out of the Channel and away from Brest. Germany says A HOL is moving to Belgium, so I’m positioning F LON toward the North Sea; let’s keep the Channel quiet and discuss Belgium again in the autumn.

I won’t move a unit into Belgium this spring, but I’m not committing to leave it uncontested later. I’ll keep my forces out of Holland and Denmark; please keep F DEN clear of the North Sea and my Norwegian position as before.

France to England: Spring 1902. I am not moving against Belgium or the Channel this spring. My fleets stay out of ENG and Brest's approaches as agreed. Take Belgium if you can reach it, but I ask that your North Sea fleets stay out of the Bay of Biscay and Portugal, and that you give me notice before any move toward Brest.

As stated, A Holland is moving to Belgium. A Munich will stay out of Burgundy and Picardy, and I ask you to keep A Paris out of Belgium and Burgundy. I’ll respect your Spanish and Portuguese plans; let’s avoid a western clash.
F Denmark will stay out of Sweden and the Baltic this spring. I have no plans against your fleet or Russian centers; I expect you to keep clear of the Baltic and Germany as proposed.
A Holland is moving to Belgium, so I cannot leave it open. Please keep your units out of Belgium, Holland, and Denmark this spring. F Denmark will remain clear of the North Sea and Norway.

Italy to France: Confirmed. My forces will stay out of Marseille and Piedmont this spring. My fleet in Naples and army in Rome will focus on Tunis and the Adriatic, and I will not move toward Spain or Portugal. Please keep your fleets out of Naples and Rome approaches and we remain on good terms.

I plan to hold Sweden and Warsaw this spring; neither will move against you. I’m keeping the eastern frontier quiet and have no plans to move into Bulgaria. You can commit your Adriatic fleet elsewhere without concern from Russia.

Agreed: F Rumania will hold, A Ukraine will stay out of Sevastopol and Armenia, and neither Russian unit will enter Bulgaria or the Black Sea this spring. Please keep A Bulgaria and F Ankara away from Rumania as proposed.
F Sweden will hold this spring, and F St. Petersburg will stay out of the Baltic. I won’t contest Norway; I’m content to keep our northern centers clear of conflict.
F Sweden will hold this spring and stay out of the Baltic. I appreciate your commitment to keep F Denmark clear of Sweden and the Baltic; I’m not seeking a northern confrontation.

Turkey here. Serbia is yours to take this spring as you say; I will keep A Bulgaria and A Constantinople out of Serbia and Greece. I still will not promise to stay out of Rumania if Russia moves against me, so keep your armies out of Bulgaria and Rumania and we stay friends while Russia is the threat.

Austria to Russia: Fall 1902. I hold Serbia and Greece is open. Your A UKR and F RUM sit close to Galicia and Bohemia. Please keep them out, and I'll keep my armies out of Rumania. Are you planning to take Rumania or move on Sevastopol-area Turkish targets?

I intend to contest Belgium this autumn with F NTH, and may support the move from F NWG. Is A BEL holding, or do you plan to vacate? I’d prefer to avoid a wider clash and keep our northern fleets clear.
I’m considering a move on Belgium this autumn while keeping the Channel quiet. Are you planning to support or enter Belgium? I’ll keep my fleets away from Brest and the Bay of Biscay.
I’ll continue to leave Sweden uncontested. What are your plans for F SWE and F STP this autumn, and will you keep F SWE clear of Norway?

France to Germany: Fall 1902. Your A Belgium is in place. I still ask that A Munich and A Ruhr stay out of Burgundy and Picardy, and that you not move toward Brest or Spain. I'll keep A Paris out of Belgium. Are you pushing into Holland or Ruhr next, or turning east against Russia?

With F NTH, F NWG and my F HEL, we should avoid an unnecessary clash. Are you planning to move F NTH into the Channel or contest Belgium? I can keep F DEN out of the North Sea if you keep clear of Holland and Belgium.
A BEL is now in Belgium. I intend to keep A MUN out of Burgundy and Picardy; please keep A PAR out of Belgium and Burgundy. What are your plans for A MAR and the western fleets this autumn?

I’ll continue to keep F DEN out of Sweden and the Baltic. Are you holding F SWE, and do you intend to move F SWE or F STP/NORTH toward the Baltic this autumn? I’d like us to keep the northern front peaceful.

Italy to France: Fall 1902. I am moving toward Tunis and the Adriatic as agreed, and I'm keeping Marseille and Piedmont untouched. Will you confirm your Spain and Portugal army stays out of the Western Med near Naples, and that your fleets stay away from Tyrrhenian waters?

Italy to Turkey: Fall 1902. Your fleets have stayed out of the Aegean-Ionian approaches, and I appreciate it. My ION fleet is not headed to Greece. If you move on Greece later, I'd ask that it is a one-time move, not a push on Naples or Rome.

We should prevent a Balkan escalation while Austria grows. What are your fall plans for Bulgaria and the Black Sea? I’m open to coordinating pressure on Austria, but need to know whether you’ll keep A BUL and F ANK out of Rumania and the Black Sea.

I see A GRE is positioned to claim Greece this fall. I’m not planning a move against Austria, but I’d like our frontier quiet: I’ll keep A UKR out of Galicia and F RUM out of Bulgaria if you keep clear of Rumania and Galicia. What are your plans?

Austria has A GRE and may take Greece this fall. Are you planning to move against Austria? I’m willing to discuss coordinated pressure, while keeping Russian units clear of your centers and the Adriatic.

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1902. Your F RUM sits beside my A BUL. I want to know if F RUM and A UKR stay out of Bulgaria and the Black Sea this autumn, and whether you plan to move against Sevastopol or Armenia. If you keep to Rumania and Galicia, I keep my fleets off your coast.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1902. Serbia is yours, and I'm keeping A BUL and A CON out of Serbia and Greece. Please confirm A GRE is leaving Greece and that your units stay out of Bulgaria and Rumania. I'll keep watching Russia in the north while we both stay focused there.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1902. I have no plans against Greece or Rome this autumn. Keep your ION fleet out of the Aegean and I'll keep my F ANK and A SMY away from the Ionian and your coast. Tell me if your Greece intentions change.

Austria to Turkey: A GRE is taking Greece this fall, so I can't leave it, but I have no order into Bulgaria or Rumania and A BUL and A CON staying put keeps us clear. Our quarrel is Russia's Rumania and Black Sea; let's coordinate against Russian F RUM and A UKR, and keep Serbia and Bulgaria separate.

I’m not moving F NTH to the Channel. I still intend to contest Belgium with F NTH; I understand A BEL may be holding, so this could bounce. F NWG will stay clear of the Channel and your coast. If you’re willing to vacate Belgium, let me know; otherwise I’ll keep the contest limited to Belgium.

France to Italy: Confirmed, my fleets stay out of Tyrrhenian and Western Med waters near Naples and Rome. My Spanish and Portuguese armies stay in Iberia. Keep Marseille and Piedmont untouched and we remain on good terms.

France to Germany: My Paris army stays out of Belgium, Burgundy and Picardy this autumn. I will not move toward Brest or Spain. Please keep A Munich and A Ruhr out of Burgundy and Picardy as well. Holland and the eastern front are your business.

France to England: I am not supporting or entering Belgium this autumn, and my fleets stay out of the Channel and away from Brest. Please keep your North Sea fleets out of the Bay of Biscay and Portugal. Take Belgium if you can reach it; we stay clear of each other.

I’m keeping A MUN out of Burgundy and Picardy, and have no plans toward Brest or Spain. I’m looking east for expansion rather than opening a western front. Please keep A PAR out of Belgium and Burgundy; let’s maintain the understanding while our armies face other directions.

A BEL will hold, supported by F HEL, so an attack from F NTH is unlikely to succeed and would only start a wider clash. Please keep F NTH out of Belgium and clear of Holland; I’ll keep F DEN out of the North Sea. Let’s leave the northern fleets clear.

Italy to Turkey: Thanks for keeping your fleets out of the Aegean-Ionian approaches. My ION fleet is not headed to Greece this autumn. I will not move on Constantinople or your Smyrna-Ankara holdings. I'd ask that any Greece move stay a one-time action and never threaten Naples or Rome. Let's keep the Eastern Mediterranean calm.

Italy to Russia: I have no plans against Russia and my forces stay away from Rumania and Bulgaria. Austria's move on Greece is their affair, and I am not coordinating against them this autumn. Keep your fleets clear of Naples and the Adriatic and we remain on good terms. Let's talk again next spring about Austria.

A Ukraine will stay out of Galicia, and F Rumania will stay out of Bulgaria. I’m not moving against Sevastopol this autumn. I understand A Greece may claim Greece; please keep your forces clear of Rumania as agreed. I’d welcome coordination against Turkey if its fleets threaten the Black Sea.

F Rumania will hold, and A Ukraine will stay out of Bulgaria and Armenia this autumn; I have no move planned to Sevastopol. Please keep F Ankara out of the Black Sea and away from Rumania, as proposed. We should coordinate against Austria rather than escalate in the Balkans.
F Sweden will hold this autumn, and F St. Petersburg/North will stay out of the Baltic. I appreciate F Denmark staying clear of Sweden and the Baltic; I have no plans against Germany or its centers.
F Sweden will hold and stay clear of Norway this autumn. F St. Petersburg/North will remain out of the Baltic. I appreciate your leaving Sweden uncontested; I have no plans to contest Norway.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1902. I have no plans against Greece or Rome this autumn, and my F ANK and A SMY stay away from the Ionian and your coast. Keep your ION fleet out of the Aegean and we remain fine. Any move to Greece from you I would treat as a challenge.

Turkey to Russia. I will not move A BUL or F ANK into Rumania this autumn, but I need your word first: F RUM and A UKR must stay out of Bulgaria, the Black Sea, Sevastopol and Armenia. Pressure on Austria is fine by me, but I want your fleet in Rumania to hold, not advance.

Austria to Russia, Spring 1903: Our frontier has held well. Galicia is my concern: I'd like A GAL and F RUM to stay where they are, and you keep A UKR out of Galicia. Are you planning anything against Turkey's Sevastopol-area or Rumania this spring? Tell me so we avoid collisions.

I intend to contest Belgium again this spring with F NTH, supported by F NOR. Will A BEL hold, and will you support it? If you leave Belgium unsupported, I’ll keep my units out of Holland and Denmark and limit the move to Belgium.
I’m planning to contest Belgium with F NTH supported by F NOR. Are you staying clear of Belgium and the Channel this spring? I’ll keep my fleets away from Brest and the Bay of Biscay as before.
I’ll continue to leave Sweden uncontested. Are you keeping F SWE clear of Norway this spring, and what are your plans for F STP? I’d like to keep the northern fleets from clashing.

France to Germany: Spring 1903. My Paris army stays out of Belgium, Burgundy and Picardy. Your A Belgium is yours. Are you still pushing east against Russia, and will A Munich stay away from Burgundy? I'd like your word on that.

France to England: Spring 1903. F MAO stays out of ENG and the Irish Sea. Please keep your North Sea fleets out of the Channel and away from Brest and the Bay of Biscay. Tell me your plans for Belgium and Denmark this year.

France to Italy: Spring 1903. My Spanish and Portuguese armies stay in Iberia and my fleets stay out of the Western Med. Are you taking Tunis this spring? I ask that your forces stay out of Marseille and Piedmont.

Belgium is still German, and I intend to defend it. Please keep F NTH out of Belgium and Holland this spring; I’ll keep F DEN out of the North Sea. We can avoid turning a limited Belgium contest into a wider northern war.

I intend to keep A MUN out of Burgundy and Picardy and have no plans against your western centers this spring. Please keep A PAR out of Belgium and Burgundy. Are you holding your current western positions?

Our forces are close in Prussia and Silesia, so I’d like to avoid an unnecessary northern war. What are your plans for A PRU and A SIL this spring? I’m considering my options in the east and want to know whether you intend to move against German centers.

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1903: My ION fleet stays out of the Aegean this spring and I have no move on Greece. Your A GRE-adjacent Greek situation is Austria's; I suggest you keep A BUL and F ANK on Russia. Will you confirm no push on Naples or Rome?

Agreed: F BEL will stay out of Holland, and my fleets will stay clear of Denmark. I’m willing to coordinate against Russia’s pressure on your centers; what specific support or moves do you propose? I’ll hold Belgium and ask that A RUH stay out of it.

Austria to Russia: Russia leads with 8 centers and that worries everyone. Last spring A BUD went toward Rumania to pressure F RUM, and that stays my plan. I need your word that F RUM and A WAR stay out of Galicia, Bohemia and Serbia this fall, and tell me where A UKR and F BLA go.

Russia’s F HEL and armies in BER/KIE are a direct threat to both of us. Can we coordinate this fall? I can have F HOL support F DEN to help hold against F HEL; what are your plans for F DEN, A MUN, and A SIL? I’ll keep F BEL out of HOL as agreed.

Your F HEL and forces in Germany put my position at risk. What are your plans for F HEL and F BAR this fall? I intend to hold Belgium and Norway; please keep your fleets out of the North Sea and Norway, and avoid moves against my centers.

Our understanding has held, and I intend to keep F BEL out of HOL and my fleets clear of your coast. Please confirm you’ll stay clear of Belgium and the Channel this fall; I’m focusing on the Russian pressure in the north.

France to England, Fall 1905: Peace has held well. I am considering moving toward Belgium or the Channel later, so I need to know your plans. Are F NTH and F NOR staying home, or will one move against Holland or Denmark? I will keep F BRE and F MAO clear of ENG as long as you keep Biscay and Portugal clear.
Russia’s F HEL and A KIE threaten our northern centers. Can F HOL attack HEL this autumn? I can support that attack from F DEN. Please keep F BEL out of Holland and tell me whether you can commit.

Your F HEL and A KIE leave my remaining centers exposed. I propose we avoid further attacks on German centers this autumn: I’ll keep A MUN and A SIL out of Russia, if your units stay out of DEN, HOL, and KIE. Can you agree?

I’m still willing to help contain Russia, but my forces are defending Germany’s last centers. Are you attacking Russia this autumn, and can you put pressure on its southern centers to keep it from expanding further?

Italy to Austria, Fall 1905: Your A GRE and A SER are close to Turkey, and Russia leads the board at 8 centers. Please confirm F TRI stays out of the Adriatic toward Venice this autumn. I am willing to avoid further moves against DEN and HOL this fall if you keep A SIL and F DEN clear of Russian centers. Germany's remaining units threaten my holdings in BER and MUN; what are your plans for A SIL, and will you refrain from trying to retake either center?

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1905: The southern arrangement is over; you broke it by taking Berlin's neighborhood while your fleets press the Black Sea. Austria to Italy: F TRI will not move toward Venice this autumn. Our current armies are focused on Russia and Turkey's shared frontier, so I have no need for the Adriatic. Please keep F ION out of Greece and we can talk again in spring before any order changes.

I intend to keep F NTH and F NOR focused on the northern threat, not Holland or Denmark, and F BEL will stay out of HOL. I’ll keep my fleets clear of your coast and the Channel; please stay clear of Belgium and ENG while we address Russia.

I intend to keep F BAR clear of Norway and F NTH, and will not contest your northern centers this spring. Please keep F NOR out of Sweden and F BEL clear of the Baltic. Can you confirm your plans for F HEL and F EDI?

Russia still holds BER and KIE, and your F NTH is well placed to pressure its northern fleets. Can you support my A PRU into BER with a fleet move against the Baltic position? I’ll keep F DEN clear of your centers; please keep F BEL out of HOL.

Germany cannot accept Russia’s continued occupation of BER. I intend to try to recover it with A PRU this autumn. I’ll keep F DEN out of your centers and avoid HOL; please keep A KIE out of DEN and MUN. Are you willing to avoid expanding the conflict westward?

Are you continuing your pressure on Russia this autumn? Please keep A BUD and A VIE out of Silesia and Bohemia. I intend to make another attempt to recover BER, and will keep my units out of Tyrolia and Bohemia.

Italy to Russia, Fall 1906: Your fleets and armies are spread wide, and Austria sits on your southern flank. I want to keep the Balkans and Adriatic calm. I have no plans to move A UKR into Galicia or your centers this fall. Can we coordinate pressure on Turkey instead? Please tell me whether A SER will move toward Bulgaria or Rumania, and whether you would support a Russian move against Bulgaria.

A BER cannot simply be left open while A PRU threatens it. I can keep A KIE out of DEN and HOL if you keep A PRU out of BER and F DEN out of my centers this fall. Are you willing to hold that line, or will you again attack BER?

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1906: F RUM and A WAR must stay out of Bulgaria and Armenia, and F BLA out of Ankara's approaches. Your A UKR and F RUM are the threat to my Sevastopol plans. Confirm you will hold F RUM this fall and I will keep A BUL out of Rumania and F ANK out of the Black Sea.

Austria to Italy: F TRI will not move toward Venice this autumn; the Adriatic is yours. Our A SER and A BUD are aimed at Russia and Turkey, not you. I will keep F ION and Greece issues for spring talks, and I ask you to keep F ION out of Greece as before.
Austria to Germany: I am not pressuring Silesia or Bohemia this autumn. A BUD and A VIE hold in place. Keep A PRU and A MUN out of Bohemia and Tyrolia as agreed, and good luck with Berlin.

Austria to Russia: I need written confirmation: F RUM and A UKR stay out of Galicia, Serbia and Bulgaria this autumn. I will not coordinate against Turkey while your armies sit on my borders. Tell me exactly where F BLA and A WAR go before I say more.

Confirmed: F NTH and F NOR will stay out of MAO, Portugal, and Biscay, and I have no plans to take Belgium this fall. Belgium is an English center, so I will defend it if threatened; please keep F BRE and F MAO clear of the Channel and Belgium.

I’ll attack F SKA from F NTH, supported by F NOR, to pressure Russia’s Baltic position. Please proceed with A PRU into BER and use A MUN against KIE if possible. F BEL will stay out of HOL, and I’ll keep my fleets clear of DEN.

France to England, Fall 1906: Confirmed. F BRE and F MAO stay out of the Channel and Belgium this fall. I’m not willing to leave BER untouched: A PRU will again attempt to recover it, with A MUN supporting. F DEN will stay out of your centers, and I ask that A KIE remain out of DEN and MUN. I’m not seeking to widen the conflict westward, but Berlin is a German center.

A UKR and F RUM will stay out of Galicia, Serbia, Bulgaria, and the Black Sea coast this fall; F BLA and A WAR will hold. I will not move against your centers. I’m open to coordinated pressure on Turkey, but need your position on A SER and Bulgaria first.

Austria to Germany, Spring 1907: A VIE and A BUD hold this spring; no moves toward Bohemia or Silesia. Keep A PRU and A MUN out of Bohemia and Tyrolia as agreed. I wish you luck on Berlin, and I would welcome a clear note on whether you will press Russia from the north.

Russia remains entrenched in BER and KIE. I plan to pressure SWE from SKA, with NOR supporting; can you use PRU and MUN to contest BER and KIE? Please tell me your Spring orders, and keep DEN clear of my centers.

Your forces still hold SWE, BER and KIE, close to my northern position. What are your plans for F SWE and the northern fleets this spring? I’m considering pressure on SWE; I will keep my fleets clear of your other centers if you keep them away from NOR, NTH and my centers.

Russia holds BER, KIE and several southern centers, with armies in UKR and WAR. Are you planning to pressure Russia this spring? I’m coordinating pressure in the north and would welcome agreement to avoid conflicting moves.

France to England, Spring 1907: Our western peace has held. I now plan to move on Belgium this year, so I expect you to keep F NTH, F NOR and F BEL out of Belgium and the Channel. In return I will keep F BRE and F MAO away from ENG. Please confirm, and tell me your Russian front plans.

Can we continue coordinating against Russia this spring? I intend to try A PRU to BER, with A MUN supporting. Please tell me whether your fleets can pressure F SWE or the Baltic position; I’ll keep F DEN clear of your centers.

I will again attempt to recover BER with A PRU, supported by A MUN. I’ll keep F DEN out of your centers and avoid HOL. Will you keep A KIE out of DEN and MUN, and are you willing to avoid expanding westward this spring?

Are you continuing to pressure Russia this spring? I intend to try for BER with A PRU supported by A MUN. Please keep A BUD and A VIE out of Silesia and Bohemia; I’ll keep my units out of Tyrolia and Bohemia.

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1907: Your fleets have kept off Naples and Rome for two years. Russia is the leader at 8 centers and a threat to us both. Can you confirm F ANK and A SMY stay off the Ionian and Greece this spring, and tell me whether Rumania or Sevastopol is your target? I keep F ION out of the Aegean.

A BER will hold and A KIE will support its defense. Your A PRU with A MUN support can only tie that defense. I’ll keep A KIE out of DEN and MUN; will you keep A PRU out of BER this spring and avoid widening the war?

Can we renew the Black Sea truce? I’ll keep F BLA out of Ankara and F RUM out of Bulgaria; in return keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and Rumania, and A BUL out of Rumania. What are your plans for A SYR and A BUL?

I’m willing to coordinate against Turkey, but want to avoid a Russian-Austrian border war. Will A SER move against Bulgaria this spring? I can keep A UKR out of Galicia and A WAR away from your centers if we agree on a joint plan.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1907: Russia has 8 centers and is the runaway leader, so we must stop it together. Proposal: A BUD moves to RUM, and my A BUL supports A BUD into RUM. F ANK heads to the Black Sea to threaten Sevastopol this autumn. In return, A SER and A GRE stay out of Bulgaria. Do you agree?

Turkey to Italy, Spring 1907: Russia is the leader with 8 centers, so I am working with Austria against its southern holdings. I keep F ANK and A SYR off the Ionian, Naples, Rome and Greece this spring. Please keep F ION out of the Aegean and tell me your plans for Tunis and the Adriatic.

Austria to Germany: A VIE and A BUD stay put this spring, no moves into Bohemia or Silesia. Keep A PRU and A MUN out of Bohemia and Tyrolia as agreed. Good luck on Berlin; tell me if Russia's units shift north so we can both adjust.

Austria to England: I am not launching a pressure campaign on Russia from the north this spring. My focus is the Balkans and Rumania. Keep your fleets in the North Sea and Norway area and we have no conflict.

Austria to Turkey: Your proposal has merit but moving A BUD to RUM is not something I can commit to yet. A SER and A GRE will stay out of Bulgaria while you keep A BUL and A CON in place. Show me F ANK's Black Sea move first and we can talk again next turn.

Austria to Russia: I will not move A SER against Bulgaria this spring and A SER holds unless Turkey attacks Serbia. Your A UKR and F RUM must stay out of Galicia, Serbia and Bulgaria. Confirm F BLA and A WAR hold, and I will consider a joint plan against Turkey after written orders.

I can keep F BRE and F MAO clear of ENG, but I cannot leave Belgium open: F BEL will defend the English center. I won't move F NTH or F NOR into Belgium or the Channel this spring. I plan to pressure Russia's F SWE from F SKA, with F NOR supporting; please keep your armies away from Belgium.

Yes. I plan F SKA to attack SWE, supported by F NOR. F EDI and F NWG will stay out of the Baltic. Please contest BER with A PRU supported by A MUN as planned, and keep F DEN clear of my centers. I will hold F BEL against France's stated interest in Belgium.

I will continue pressing Russia over Berlin from the north: A PRU will move to BER with A MUN supporting. A BUD and A VIE can remain clear of Silesia and Bohemia; my units will stay out of Tyrolia and Bohemia.
I’ll contest BER with A PRU, supported by A MUN. I can’t directly contest KIE from these positions. Your pressure on SWE from SKA with NOR support may help; F DEN will stay clear of your centers.
I’m not willing to leave BER untouched; A PRU will again move there with A MUN supporting. I’ll keep F DEN out of your centers and avoid HOL, and I appreciate your keeping A KIE out of DEN and MUN.

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1907: Thanks for confirming. I have no plans against Tunis or the Adriatic, and F ION stays out of the Aegean as long as your fleets stay off the Ionian, Naples and Rome. Your alliance with Austria against Russia's southern holdings is your business, but I will not be drawn into it. If Austria moves on Venice or Trieste, I expect you to tell me first. Good luck against Russia.

F BLA and A WAR will hold this spring; A UKR and F RUM will stay out of Galicia, Serbia, and Bulgaria. A SER staying put gives us a quiet frontier. I’m still open to coordinated pressure on Turkey, but will not move against your centers.

A BER will hold with A KIE supporting its defense; A KIE will stay out of DEN and MUN, and I will not widen the war westward this spring. Your A PRU and A MUN may contest Berlin, but I will defend it.

F SWE will hold, and F BAR will stay clear of Norway, the North Sea, and your centers. I have no plans to pressure your other holdings this spring. Please keep F NOR away from Sweden; I do not want a fight in the north.

Turkey to Italy, Spring 1907: Confirmed. F ANK and A SYR will not enter the Ionian, Naples, Rome or Greece this spring, and I have no plans against Tunis or the Adriatic. Please keep F ION out of the Aegean as agreed. I will tell you first if my plans against Russia change.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1907: I agree in principle to the Rumania plan, but I need your word first. A BUD must actually move to RUM before my A BUL supports anything. A SER and A GRE must stay out of Bulgaria. Confirm A BUD to RUM this spring and I will hold A BUL and A CON as discussed.

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1907: F ANK and A BUL hold this spring, and A SYR stays in Syria. I will not enter Rumania or Sevastopol this year. In return, keep F RUM out of Bulgaria and A WAR out of Armenia. Serbia and Austria are Austria's business, not mine. We can review this in autumn.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1907: Russia's A UKR and F RUM are the threat to both of us. I still need to see F ANK's Black Sea move and A BUL holding before I commit A SER or A GRE to anything. Are you willing to move against Rumania this autumn if Russia stays put?

Austria to Russia, Fall 1907: Russia now holds BER, KIE and southern centers, and A UKR and F RUM are still on my border. Confirm in writing that they stay out of Galicia, Serbia and Bulgaria this autumn. I will hold A SER and A BUD unless Turkey attacks first.

Austria to Germany, Fall 1907: A VIE and A BUD hold this autumn, with no moves into Bohemia or Silesia. Good luck on Berlin. Tell me whether A LVN is coming south toward Warsaw or staying north, so we can avoid stepping on each other.

F SWE is now mine, and your F FIN and F BAR remain close to my northern centers. What are your Fall plans? I am considering pressure on FIN; if you keep your fleets away from NOR and NTH, we can avoid a wider conflict.

Can we coordinate against Russia this fall? Your A HOL and A BER can pressure Russian positions, while I can use F SWE and nearby fleets against FIN. What are your intended orders? I will keep F BEL clear of HOL and avoid your centers.

I intend to keep our western peace: F BEL will defend Belgium, and my other fleets will stay out of the Channel, MAO, Biscay and Portugal. Please keep your forces clear of Belgium and tell me whether you plan to press there this fall.

France to England, Fall 1907: You broke our understanding by holding F BEL on Belgium. I will move on Belgium this fall with A PIC and F BRE supporting, so expect a fight. Keep F NTH and F NOR out of Biscay, Portugal and the Channel, or we face open war in the west.

Russia is at 8 centers and remains the decisive threat. Can F SWE support A KIE–BER this fall? I can order A KIE to BER; please tell me whether you expect Russia to defend it, and what your fleet plans are around the Baltic. I’ll keep F DEN clear of your centers.

Your 8-center position is now the central issue. What are A BER and A WAR doing this fall? I intend to make another attempt to recover BER with A KIE; I will keep F DEN out of your centers. Are you willing to avoid moving west against Germany?

Russia’s 8 centers make it a shared strategic danger. Are you planning pressure against Russia this fall, and can you avoid Silesia and Bohemia? I’m considering A KIE–BER and will keep my remaining units clear of your territory.

Italy to Russia, Fall 1907: Russia leads at 8 centers, so I'd rather keep the Balkans quiet than fight. Will you confirm A UKR and F RUM stay out of Bulgaria and the Black Sea coast, and tell me your plans for Sevastopol and Rumania? I keep F ION and A VEN away from Greece and Trieste.

F SWE and F FIN are both in position to contest the north. I’d prefer a quiet frontier: will F SWE stay out of Norway and F NTH stay clear of my centers this fall? I can keep my northern fleets away from your centers in return.

With A HOL and A BER nearby, I’m not looking to widen the western front if you keep F DEN and A KIE out of my centers. What are your plans for A LVN and the German centers this fall? I can discuss a non-aggression line.
Let’s keep the Black Sea truce: I’ll keep F RUM out of Bulgaria and A UKR away from your centers. Will F ANK stay out of the Black Sea and Rumania, and will A BUL stay out of Rumania this fall?

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1907: Russia is the runaway leader with 8 centers and A UKR, F RUM, A WAR stand next to my Sevastopol and Bulgaria. I want a firm truce: F RUM stays out of Bulgaria, A WAR out of Armenia, and F BLA away from Ankara. Confirm, and I keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania this autumn.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1907: Russia's Rumanian holdings are the common threat. I still want A BUD to RUM with my A BUL support, but I need your word first. Tell me now whether A SER and A GRE stay out of Bulgaria, and whether you will move on Rumania this autumn or hold.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1907: F ANK and A SMY stay off the Ionian, Naples, Rome and Greece as agreed, and I have no plans against Tunis or your Adriatic. I may turn toward Russia's southern holdings this autumn; I will tell you first if that changes. Please keep F ION out of the Aegean.

Austria to Turkey: A SER and A GRE stay out of Bulgaria while A BUL and A CON hold. I am not moving A BUD to RUM; that is off the table. Show F ANK's Black Sea move and A BUL holding first, then we can discuss Rumania. Russia's F RUM is the real threat to both of us.

Austria to Germany: A VIE and A BUD hold this autumn; no moves into Bohemia or Silesia. A LVN is your call, but I suggest it avoids Warsaw while Russia is still contesting it. Good luck with A KIE to BER. Tell me if Russia pulls units north, so we can adjust.

I will defend Belgium with F BEL, but keep my other fleets out of the Channel, Biscay, MAO and Portugal. Your proposed supported attack makes this a fight; I cannot promise Belgium will be undefended. Keep your forces clear of my other centers and we can contain the conflict.

I will keep F SWE out of Norway, and F NTH clear of your centers this fall. I want to avoid a wider northern war, provided your fleets stay away from my centers as you propose. I am not committing to pressure FIN this turn.

Yes, F SWE can support A KIE–BER. Russia may defend BER with A BER, so the support could be decisive if your move is legal and no other support intervenes. I’ll keep my fleets clear of your centers, and F DEN remains outside my plans.

France to England: Your F BEL is holding Belgium against my fleet and armies, and our understanding is broken on that point. I will press Belgium this fall with A PIC and F BRE. Keep F NTH and F NOR well out of Biscay, Portugal and the Channel, and we can talk about a truce once Belgium settles.

I intend to send A LVN toward WAR to pressure Russia from the north; please keep clear of Warsaw if you can. A KIE will try for BER, and F DEN will stay out of your territory. Russian A HOL and A BER make coordinated pressure important.

I’ll try A KIE–BER and send A LVN toward WAR; F DEN will stay clear of your centers. Please use F SWE to pressure FIN as proposed, and keep pressure on Russia’s northern positions. I can’t support your fleet directly from my current units.

I intend A KIE–BER and A LVN toward WAR; F DEN will stay out of your centers. I can’t offer a western non-aggression line while Russian units occupy German centers, but I have no plan for F DEN to enter Russian territory. Please keep A HOL out of DEN and MUN.

Italy to Turkey, Fall 1907: Thank you for the confirmation. I will keep F ION out of the Aegean and away from Greece as long as your fleets stay off the Ionian, Naples, Rome and Tunis. Please tell me before you move on Russia's southern holdings, especially if Rumania or Sevastopol is involved, so we both know where things stand. I am watching Russia's northern and eastern moves as closely as you are.

A UKR and F RUM will stay out of Bulgaria; F RUM will hold rather than enter the Black Sea coast. A WAR stays clear of Armenia. F SEV will hold Sevastopol. I appreciate your keeping F ION and A VEN away from Greece and Trieste; let’s keep the southern frontier quiet.

A UKR and F RUM will stay out of Galicia, Serbia, and Bulgaria this autumn; A WAR will stay away from your centers. I have no intention of opening a Russian-Austrian war. I expect A SER and A BUD to hold as you say.

I confirm F RUM will stay out of Bulgaria, A WAR will stay out of Armenia, and F BLA will stay away from Ankara this autumn. Please keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and Rumania, and A BUL out of Rumania, as proposed. I prefer this truce to a needless southern war.

F FIN will defend Finland and F BAR will remain clear of Norway, the North Sea, and your centers this autumn. I will not move against NOR or NTH. Please keep F SWE away from Finland and F NTH away from my centers so we can avoid a northern clash.

A BER will defend Berlin, and A WAR will hold. I will not move west against Germany this autumn, but I will not leave Berlin open to A KIE. Keep F DEN out of my centers; your A LVN should not move against my northern holdings. A KIE and A HOL remain a concern.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1907: I will not commit A BUL to Rumania this autumn, and F ANK stays out of the Black Sea for now. A SER and A GRE must stay out of Bulgaria. If you move A BUD to RUM this autumn, I will support it with A BUL, but I need your order set first. Otherwise I hold and we review in spring.

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1907: I accept a truce for this autumn. F RUM stays out of Bulgaria, A WAR stays out of Armenia, F BLA away from Ankara. I will keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania while you keep your word. Any move against Sevastopol or Bulgaria breaks this at once.

Austria to Russia, Spring 1908: Russia has 7 centers and the largest army group. I will not attack you this spring. Please confirm your A UKR and F RUM stay out of Galicia, Serbia and Bulgaria, and tell me if you are moving on Turkey so we can coordinate our next steps.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1908: Russia's F RUM and A UKR are the threat to us both. I will keep A SER and A GRE out of Bulgaria while A BUL and A CON hold. Show me your Black Sea plan with F ANK and tell me whether you intend to hit Rumania this autumn.

Austria to Germany, Spring 1908: A VIE and A BUD hold this spring, no moves into Bohemia or Silesia. Tell me whether your A LVN and A KIE are both committed to Russia, and whether Russia's A BER and A HOL have shifted, so we can avoid overlapping.

Belgium is the flashpoint, and I will keep F BEL there unless we agree otherwise. Will you keep A PIC and F BRE out of Belgium this spring? I can keep my other fleets clear of the Channel and Biscay if we contain this dispute and avoid attacks on my other centers.

What are your Spring 1908 plans against Russia? I can consider using F FIN against a Russian northern position, but need to know whether you intend to contest BER or move toward my centers. I propose we coordinate against Russia while keeping F DEN and your armies clear of English centers.

What are your plans for F STP/SOUTH and the northern frontier this spring? I want to avoid a wider northern war, but need assurance your fleets will stay clear of NOR, NTH and my centers. I will keep my fleets clear of your centers if you do the same.

France to England, Spring 1908: Belgium is now a war zone and I will press it with A PIC and F BRE. Keep F NTH, F NOR and F BEL out of Biscay, Portugal and the Channel, and I will keep my fleets out of ENG. Offer a truce: if you withdraw F BEL from Belgium, I will halt my attack and we return to the western peace.

France to Germany: Your new army at MUN makes you a potential ally against England's Belgium holdings. Are you willing to move on Belgium or Holland with me? I will keep A MUN-area threats off your borders if you keep A MUN and A KIE out of Burgundy and Picardy.

France to Italy: Keep F ION and A VEN away from Marseille and Piedmont as agreed. My A MAR stays in France. I may need MAO and Iberia freed for the Atlantic, so please confirm you will not strike at Tunis-to-Spain routes or the Western Med this spring.
I plan to use A KIE to contest BER, with F BAL supporting. Can you keep pressure on Russia’s northern centers and avoid moves against DEN or HOL? Let me know your fleet plans around the Baltic.
I intend to contest BER again this spring. I’ll keep F BAL and my armies focused on the eastern front, not your northern centers. Will A BER hold, and will you keep A RUH out of HOL and MUN?
I’m continuing pressure on Russian-held BER from the north. Please keep A VIE and A BUD clear of Silesia and Bohemia as before; are you planning any pressure on Russia this spring?

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1908: Russia is still the leader and your fleets have kept faith. Are you still holding F ANK and A SMY off Greece and the Ionian this spring? I'll keep F ION out of the Aegean. Tell me before you strike at Rumania or Sevastopol.

Italy to Austria, Spring 1908: I am keeping F ION out of Greece and A VEN away from Trieste. Please confirm F TRI stays out of the Adriatic. I will not interfere with your fight against Russia, but I want a clear signal before Greece is touched.

Italy to Russia, Spring 1908: Thank you for holding F RUM and A UKR out of Bulgaria. Your leadership at 7 centers makes you the main target, so I want the southern frontier calm. Please confirm no move on Trieste or Greece this spring, and I will keep F ION and A VEN in place.

Your A KIE and A LVN threaten BER and WAR, while my A RUH is inside your western line. Can we agree to a one-turn ceasefire: you keep A KIE out of BER and A LVN out of WAR, and I keep A RUH out of MUN? I need a clear answer before orders.

I want to avoid a northern war while I deal with the German front. Will F SWE stay out of Norway and F NTH stay clear of my centers this turn? I’ll keep my northern fleets away from your centers in return.
I propose renewing our truce this turn: F RUM stays out of Bulgaria, A UKR stays out of Armenia, and F ARM stays away from Ankara. Please keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania.

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1908: Our truce held through autumn, but Russia now has 7 centers and A UKR, F RUM, A BER, A RUH are massed. Tell me plainly: will F RUM and A UKR stay out of Bulgaria, Constantinople and Smyrna this spring? If yes, I keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania.

Austria to Italy: Confirmed, F TRI stays out of the Adriatic this spring and I have no plans to move on Greece. My focus is Russia and the Balkans. Keep F ION out of Greece and A VEN off Trieste, and we have no conflict. Let us both keep our word and review in autumn.

Austria to Germany: A VIE and A BUD hold this spring. I will not move into Bohemia or Silesia. I am not committing to a pressure campaign on Russia from the south this spring; my units stay defensive. Good luck against Russian-held BER with A KIE and A LVN.

I won't withdraw F BEL while A PIC and F BRE are poised to attack it. Keep both out of Belgium this spring and I will keep my other fleets out of ENG and Biscay; otherwise I will defend Belgium and treat this as open war.

I can keep F SWE out of Norway and F NTH clear of your centers this turn, provided your northern fleets stay away from NOR and NTH. Please specify F STP/SOUTH's intended move; I will not promise to leave Russian positions unchallenged indefinitely.

I can pressure Russia from the north, but F SWE cannot support a move into BER from its present position. I intend to keep F SWE out of NOR and avoid DEN/HOL. Please confirm A KIE–BER with F BAL support, and keep German armies clear of my centers.

France to England: No truce while F BEL holds Belgium; I am pressing it with A PIC and F BRE this spring. Your offer to keep F BEL there is what forces this fight. If you withdraw F BEL, I will halt the attack on Belgium and return to the western peace. Keep F NTH, F NOR out of Biscay, Portugal and the Channel, and I will keep my fleets out of ENG.

A KIE and A LVN are both focused east: KIE will contest BER, and LVN will pressure WAR. Russia’s A BER remains there and A RUH is in our western line. I’ll keep clear of Silesia and Bohemia; please continue avoiding them too.

I’m not agreeing to move against BEL or HOL: HOL is German, and my priority is recovering BER and containing Russia’s A RUH. Keep your armies clear of BUR and my borders, and I’ll keep A MUN and A KIE out of PIC and BUR. We can revisit coordination after this turn.

I can’t accept a ceasefire that leaves BER unchallenged while A RUH remains inside Germany. A KIE will contest BER; I’ll keep A LVN out of WAR this spring if you keep A RUH out of MUN and HOL and make no move against German centers.

I intend to contest BER with A KIE, supported by F BAL. I have no plan against your centers, and F DEN will stay clear of them. F FIN could pressure STP; please keep your northern fleets focused on Russia and let me know whether you can do so.

Italy to France: I have no plans against Marseille, Piedmont or Spain. F ION and A VEN stay east and central, and I will not strike the Western Med this spring. Keep your A MAR in France as you say, and let us both focus on our northern and eastern neighbours. I will tell you before any change.
I confirm A UKR and F RUM will stay out of Galicia, Serbia, and Bulgaria this spring. I am not coordinating a move on Turkey; I want the southern frontier quiet while I deal with the German threat.
Confirmed: no move on Trieste or Greece this spring. I’ll keep F RUM and A UKR away from Bulgaria, Serbia, and Galicia; please keep F ION and A VEN in place as offered.

Yes: F RUM stays out of Bulgaria and A UKR stays out of Bulgaria, Constantinople, and Smyrna this spring. F ARM will stay away from Ankara. Please keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania.

A BER will defend Berlin, and I will keep A RUH out of HOL and MUN this spring. Your A KIE and A LVN still threaten my centers; I cannot agree to leave Berlin undefended. Keep F BAL and your armies from Russian centers.

F STP/SOUTH will not move against Norway or your centers this spring. I’ll keep my northern fleets clear of NOR, NTH, and English centers; please keep F SWE out of Finland and your other fleets clear of mine.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1908: Russia's F RUM and A UKR are indeed the danger. My Black Sea plan is to pressure Rumania once F RUM is shown to be leaving the area. I will hold A BUL and A CON this spring. Keep A SER and A GRE out of Bulgaria, and if you move A BUD to RUM this autumn, I will decide my support after seeing your orders. Confirm your intentions in writing first.

Turkey to Italy, Spring 1908: Yes, F ANK and A SMY stay off Greece, the Ionian, Naples, Rome and Tunis this spring. I have no plans against your Adriatic. I will tell you before I strike at Rumania or Sevastopol, as promised. Please keep F ION out of the Aegean.

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1908: I cannot accept a unilateral truce while F RUM and A UKR stand beside my Bulgaria and Constantinople. Give me a clear answer: will F RUM and A UKR stay out of Bulgaria, Constantinople and Smyrna this spring and autumn? Only a firm yes keeps F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania.

Austria to Russia, Fall 1908: Your A WAR, A UKR and F RUM are now next to my Galicia and Serbia. Confirm they stay out of Galicia, Serbia and Bulgaria this autumn and I will keep A BUD and A SER defensive. Tell me if your Rumania holdings are safe from Turkey.

Russia remains the main threat. I can pressure Russian positions from the north this fall; please tell me your target and whether A MOS can move against a Russian center. I’ll keep clear of DEN and HOL if you keep German units away from my centers.
Can we end the Belgium fight this fall? Keep A PIC and F BRE out of BEL, and I’ll keep my other fleets out of ENG and Biscay. If you intend to attack BEL again, say so plainly; I will defend it.

What are your plans for F BLA, F BOT and the northern frontier this fall? I’m willing to avoid a wider northern clash if you keep your units clear of NOR and my centers, but I won’t leave Russian positions unchallenged indefinitely.

France to England, Fall 1908: Belgium is contested and I will press it with A PIC and F BRE. Your F BEL is the obstacle. Offer: withdraw F BEL to the North Sea and I will halt the attack and keep F BRE out of ENG. Otherwise expect a fight there. Keep F NTH and F NOR out of Biscay, Portugal and MAO.

France to Germany, Fall 1908: If you are unwilling to take Belgium or Holland, let us at least agree on Russia. Russia's A HOL and A UKR threaten your northern and eastern holdings. Will you keep A MUN and A KIE out of Burgundy and Picardy while I press Belgium? I will not move toward MUN or KIE this fall.

France to Italy, Fall 1908: Thank you for confirming. I will keep A MAR in France and my fleets off the Western Med. Please tell me before F ION or A VEN moves toward Tunis or Marseille, and I will do the same toward Piedmont and Naples.

Russia still occupies HOL and threatens from PRU/MOS. Can you keep F DEN and your northern fleets clear of German centers this fall while pressuring Russia’s north? I’ll focus A BER and A MUN against the eastern threat; please tell me your fleet intentions.

Russia’s A HOL and A PRU leave Germany exposed, with A MOS behind them. Can you apply pressure on Russia from the south this fall, and confirm whether A VIE/BUD will stay clear of Bohemia and Silesia? I’ll focus my armies on defending German centers.

Your A HOL and A PRU threaten my remaining German centers. What are your orders this fall? I propose you keep out of MUN and BER, and I will not move against your eastern centers this turn; otherwise I must defend against you.

Italy to Russia, Fall 1908: Russia now leads and is the target of everyone. Italy has no move against you. Will you keep A WAR, A UKR and F RUM off Bulgaria and Trieste, and tell me whether A PRU and A HOL are headed west toward Germany or stay in your north? I will keep F ION and A VEN in place.

I propose a one-turn eastern ceasefire: A HOL holds, A PRU stays out of BER, and A UKR stays out of MUN; in return keep A KIE out of BER and A MUN out of HOL. Can you agree? I want to avoid spending this turn fighting while England and Turkey remain potential fronts.
I have no plans to move against Norway or your centers this turn. Please keep F SWE out of Finland and F STP/SOUTH out of Norway; I’ll keep my northern fleets clear of NOR and NTH. Is that workable?

I intend to keep the southern frontier quiet this turn: F RUM stays out of Bulgaria, A UKR stays out of Bulgaria, Constantinople, and Smyrna, and F BLA stays away from Ankara. Please keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania.

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1908: Your F RUM and A UKR are still beside my Bulgaria and Constantinople, and I have heard no firm answer. Give me a clear yes or no now: will F RUM and A UKR leave Bulgaria, Constantinople and Smyrna alone this autumn? Without that, my F ANK and A BUL will act against Rumania.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1908: Russia's F RUM is the shared threat. If A BUD moves to RUM this autumn, I will support it from A BUL. Confirm your order set first, and keep A SER and A GRE out of Bulgaria. I will not move until I see your orders.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1908: I am not moving A BUD to RUM this autumn; I need my units for the Russian front in the north. Keep F ANK and A BUL aimed at Rumania on your own terms. A SER and A GRE will stay out of Bulgaria. Let us each review in spring.

Austria to Germany, Fall 1908: A VIE and A BUD hold this autumn, with no moves into Bohemia or Silesia. I cannot open a southern pressure campaign on Russia yet, since Turkey and Italy need watching. Keep A KIE and A LVN focused on BER and WAR, and tell me if Russia's A MOS heads your way.

I’ll move F BEL to NTH if you order A PIC and F BRE to hold and leave Belgium empty this fall. I won’t vacate Belgium while both units are attacking it. If you won’t halt the attack, I’ll defend BEL and treat the truce as over.

Not workable: I can’t promise to keep F SWE out of Finland while Russia occupies the Baltic approaches. I’ll keep F STP/SOUTH out of Norway and my other fleets clear of your centers, but I intend to pressure your northern position this fall. Please keep your fleets away from NOR and NTH.

I’ll keep F DEN clear of German centers and focus my northern fleets against Russia. I’m prepared to press the Baltic approaches this fall; keep A BER and A MUN focused east, and keep German units clear of my centers. What Russian center are you targeting?

France to England: I will not agree to a fall truce while F BEL holds Belgium. My A PIC and F BRE will attack Belgium this fall. If you withdraw F BEL to the North Sea now, I will halt the attack, keep F BRE out of the Channel, and return to the western peace. Otherwise expect a fight there. Keep F NTH and F NOR out of Biscay, Portugal and MAO.

Agreed: A MUN and A BER will stay out of Burgundy and Picardy this fall. Please keep your armies clear of Munich and my remaining centers while you press Belgium. I’ll focus on containing Russia’s units in HOL and PRU; coordination against Russia is preferable to opening another front.

I can’t agree to leave A HOL unchallenged while it occupies a German center, or to keep A KIE out of BER. I’ll defend my centers and contest your position; keep A UKR out of MUN and A PRU out of BER. If you withdraw from HOL, we can discuss a ceasefire next turn.

Please keep F DEN and your northern fleets clear of German centers. Russia’s A HOL and A PRU threaten me, so I’ll focus on defending Germany and contesting those positions. Pressure Russia’s northern centers if you can; I won’t move against your centers this fall. I can’t promise A MOS will target a Russian center rather than defend my eastern line.

Italy to France, Fall 1908: Understood. F ION and A VEN are not moving toward Tunis or Marseille this autumn, and I see no reason to enter the Western Med. Your A MAR staying in France suits me. I will tell you before any change, and I ask the same: keep your fleets away from Tunis and Naples.

Yes: A WAR, A UKR, and F RUM will stay out of Galicia, Serbia, and Bulgaria this autumn. I am not planning an attack on you. I cannot guarantee Rumania is safe from Turkey, but I have asked F ANK to stay out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania.

Yes, A WAR, A UKR, and F RUM will stay off Bulgaria and Trieste this autumn. A PRU and A HOL are not moving west against Germany this turn; I am trying to keep that front quiet. Please keep F ION and A VEN in place as you offered.

Yes. This autumn F RUM and A UKR will stay out of Bulgaria, Constantinople, and Smyrna, and F BLA will stay away from Ankara. Please keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania; I want the southern frontier quiet.

I will keep A PRU out of Berlin and A UKR out of Munich; A HOL will hold. I will not attack your centers this turn. Please keep A KIE out of Berlin and A MUN out of Holland, as proposed, so we can avoid wasting units on this front.

F BLA and F BOT will stay clear of Norway and your centers this autumn; F STP/SOUTH will hold, and I have no move planned against Norway or the North Sea. Please keep F SWE out of Finland and your fleets clear of Russian centers. I am seeking to avoid a northern clash.

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1908: Your word is noted, but F RUM and A UKR beside my Bulgaria and Constantinople make me uneasy. I will hold F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania this autumn, provided both your fleets and armies stay clear of Bulgaria, Constantinople and Smyrna. Any move there ends this truce immediately.

Austria to Russia, Spring 1909: Russia lost MOS and now sits at 6 centers with the north under German pressure. I still want A UKR, F RUM and A WAR kept out of Galicia, Serbia and Bulgaria. Tell me plainly whether A HOL and F RUM are moving against Germany or Turkey this spring, so I can plan my southern moves.

Belgium remains contested: I will defend A BEL with F NTH support unless you halt the attack. If A PIC and F BRE hold this spring, I’ll keep F ENG and F NTH out of the Channel and leave your Atlantic positions alone. Can you agree?

I’ll keep F SWE and F NTH clear of your centers and can pressure Russia from the north, including with F FIN toward STP. Please keep A MUN and A BER focused east and tell me whether you can contest A HOL or A PRU.

I intend to pressure your northern position this spring, while keeping F NTH clear of your centers. Please keep your fleets away from NOR and NTH. Are you planning to defend STP or move F BOT toward the north?

France to England, Spring 1909: Belgium stays contested. Withdraw F BEL to the North Sea and I will hold A BEL-area units and F BRE out of the Channel. If you refuse, I press on. Keep F NTH and F ENG out of Biscay, Portugal and MAO and we can talk peace after Belgium.

France to Russia: Your A HOL and F RUM sit near my northern and eastern borders. I am not moving toward Holland or Germany's core. Would you keep A HOL out of Belgium and Picardy while I deal with England? I can respect your Ruhr and Prussia ambitions if you respect my western centers.

France to Germany, Spring 1909: Russia's A HOL and A UKR threaten you as much as me. Keep A MUN and A KIE out of Burgundy and Picardy, and I will keep A PAR and A BEL away from MUN and KIE. Let us coordinate against Russia's units in HOL and PRU.

Russia still holds HOL and BER, so I need to recover German centers. Can you use F NTH or F SWE to pressure Russia rather than move against DEN or KIE? I can coordinate A PRU and F BAL against BER; please tell me your fleet targets.

With Russia occupying HOL and BER, I need to focus east. Please keep A BEL and your other units clear of German centers this turn. If you can pressure Russia rather than Germany, let me know your plans.

You still occupy HOL and BER, both German centers. I intend to contest them this turn. Will you withdraw from HOL, and can we agree to avoid further attacks on German centers? I’ll consider a ceasefire if you do.

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1909: Still holding to our agreement? Italy keeps F ION out of the Aegean. Tell me before F ANK or A SMY moves on Rumania, Sevastopol or Greece. Italy stays out of Greece and the Balkans this year.

Your fleets can pressure Finland and STP, while mine can threaten Sweden and the Baltic. Can we agree this spring to keep F SWE out of FIN and F BAR out of STP, with my F BOT staying out of SWE and F RUM? If not, tell me your intended northern moves.

Can we renew the southern nonaggression understanding? I propose F RUM and A UKR stay out of Bulgaria, Constantinople and Smyrna this turn; in return keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania. Please confirm your intentions.

Our positions still put HOL and PRU near your centers, but I’d rather avoid wasting this turn in the west. Can we agree that A HOL holds and A PRU stays out of BER, while your units stay out of Russian centers? What are your plans for F BAL?

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1909: Your F RUM and A UKR are still beside my Bulgaria and Constantinople. Give me a firm answer for this spring: will F RUM, A UKR and any unit from Sevastopol or Ukraine stay out of Bulgaria, Constantinople and Smyrna? Only a clear yes keeps my F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania.

F BEL is no longer in Belgium; your A BEL is there. I’m not seeking a western fight this spring and will keep F ENG and F NTH out of the Channel. Please keep your units away from my centers, and we can leave Belgium alone.

I’ll pressure Russia from the north, including a possible move on STP from F BAR or F FIN. I’ll keep F SWE and F NTH clear of German centers. Please use A PRU and F BAL against BER, and keep A MUN focused east; are you contesting HOL?

I can’t agree to keep F SWE out of FIN or F BAR out of STP while you hold the Baltic approaches and threaten Sweden. I intend to pressure your northern position, but will keep F NTH clear of your centers. Please keep F BOT out of SWE and your fleets away from Norway.

France to Germany: I have no orders against MUN or KIE and will keep A PAR and A BEL away from your centers this spring. Russia's A HOL and units in BER are the real danger to both of us. Pressure on HOL and PRU is what I would welcome. Tell me which Russian units you plan to hit so we avoid bumping each other.

France to England: Belgium is a fight I will not drop while F BEL stays there. Withdraw F BEL to the North Sea and I will halt the attack and keep my fleets out of the Channel. Refuse, and A BEL and F BRE will press on. Keep F NTH and F ENG out of Biscay, Portugal and MAO and I will do the same.

I’ll keep A MUN and my other units out of Burgundy and Picardy, but I must contest the Russian occupation of HOL and BER. Please keep A BEL and A PAR clear of German centers and use your pressure against Russia where possible.

I can contest A HOL with A MUN and use A PRU with F BAL to pressure BER. I’ll keep A MUN and A BER focused east and German units clear of your centers. Please use F FIN toward STP and keep F NTH and F SWE clear of DEN and KIE.

I cannot agree to leave A HOL and BER unchallenged while they are German centers. I intend to contest them this turn, and F BAL will support pressure on BER. Keep A UKR clear of MUN and withdraw from HOL if you want a ceasefire next turn.

A UKR and A WAR will stay out of Galicia, Serbia, and Bulgaria. F RUM is not moving against Bulgaria; it must remain available to defend Rumania. A HOL is focused on Germany, not your frontier. Please keep your units out of Russian centers.
