Agreed: A HOL will stay out of Belgium and Picardy this spring. I have no plans against your western centers; I am focused on the German and northern fronts. Please keep your units out of Holland and Russian centers.

Yes: F RUM, A UKR, and any unit from Sevastopol or Ukraine will stay out of Bulgaria, Constantinople, and Smyrna this spring. In return, keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania. I need Rumania secure.

I will not withdraw from Holland this spring, and cannot promise to stop contesting German centers. I can keep A PRU out of Berlin for now; keep your units out of Russian centers. What is F BAL doing? A HOL is not advancing west.

I expect to defend STP rather than abandon the northern position. F BOT will not move to Sweden this spring, and I’ll keep my fleets clear of Norway and the North Sea. Please keep F SWE out of Finland and F BAR out of STP.

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1909: No firm yes from you yet, so no renewal. F RUM, A UKR and any Sevastopol or Ukraine unit must stay out of Bulgaria, Constantinople and Smyrna. If they do, my F ANK and A BUL stay put this spring. Any move there ends the truce and I will strike Rumania.

Turkey to Italy, Spring 1909: F ANK and A SMY stay off Greece and the Ionian this spring, and I have no move on Naples, Rome or Tunis. Keep F ION out of the Aegean as agreed. I will tell you before any move on Rumania or Sevastopol.

Austria to Russia, Fall 1909: Your A UKR and F RUM hold in Ukraine and Rumania, and A WAR stays out of Galicia. I will keep A RUM-area moves defensive. Confirm you will not take Rumania from Turkey this autumn, and tell me whether A HOL moves on Berlin or stays on Germany.
Let’s coordinate against Russia again. I can use F SWE toward FIN and F STP/NORTH to pressure STP/SOUTH; please tell me your targets for A HOL, A BER and A MOS. I’ll keep F NTH clear of DEN and KIE.

What are your plans for F BOT and the northern frontier this fall? I intend to protect my northern centers and keep F NTH clear of your centers, but I won’t promise to leave FIN or STP unpressured. Please keep F BOT away from SWE.

I’m content to avoid a western fight this fall. I’ll keep my fleets out of the Channel and your Atlantic centers; please keep your units clear of my centers. Can we leave Belgium and the Channel quiet?

France to Germany, Fall 1909: Russia's A HOL and A MOS-area pressure threaten us both. Will you commit to hitting A HOL this fall? I will keep A BEL and A PAR away from MUN and KIE and won't enter Ruhr. Tell me your fall orders so we avoid bumping.

France to England, Fall 1909: Belgium is now yours to leave alone if you keep F NTH and F ENG out of the Channel and Biscay. I will keep A BEL and F BRE off your centers. Confirm you are not moving toward Belgium or Picardy this fall and we can keep the western peace.

France to Russia: Thank you for keeping A HOL out of Belgium. I will keep my units out of Holland and your centers. In return, please keep F SEV and A UKR away from Rumania and Galicia-facing French interests, and tell me your fall plans against Germany.

Russia still threatens my eastern centers. Please keep F NTH and F SWE clear of DEN and KIE, and continue pressure on Russian positions from the north. I’ll keep my units away from your centers; what are F FIN and F STP/NORTH targeting?

Your A HOL remains in a German center, and A SIL is close to BER. I intend to recover and defend German centers. Will you withdraw A HOL and keep A SIL out of BER? I’m open to a ceasefire if you stop contesting my territory.

I have no plans against your centers. Please keep A BEL and the rest of your forces clear of MUN and my other centers this fall; Russia remains the immediate threat to Germany. What are your plans around Belgium and the German border?

Italy to Turkey, Fall 1909: Our agreement has held for two years. Italy keeps F ION out of the Aegean. Please confirm F ANK and A SMY stay off Greece and Rumania this autumn, and tell me before any strike on Sevastopol, since Russia's southern holdings matter to the balance.

I intend to contest A MOS and recover Moscow. Can we keep this limited to that front: your units stay out of Russian centers other than MOS, and I keep A HOL out of your western centers? What are your plans for A MOS and A BER?

I want to avoid a fight over STP this autumn. Will F BAR stay out of STP and F SWE stay out of Finland if F BOT stays out of Sweden and your other centers? Please tell me where your northern fleets are headed.

I propose renewing the southern truce: F ARM and F SEV stay out of Ankara, Bulgaria, Constantinople and Smyrna, and A UKR stays out of Bulgaria; in return, F ANK stays out of the Black Sea and A BUL stays out of Rumania. Can you confirm?

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1909: Your spring word held, so I will not strike yet. But F RUM and A UKR are still massed by my border. Confirm in writing that neither unit moves to Bulgaria, Constantinople, or Smyrna this autumn. If you do, F ANK and A BUL stay put. If you move against them, my truce ends at once.

Agreed: I will keep F NTH and F STP/NORTH out of the Channel and Biscay, and will not move toward Belgium or Picardy this fall. Please keep A BEL and F BRE clear of my centers; let us maintain the western peace.

F SWE will pressure FIN, and F STP/NORTH will move toward STP/SOUTH. F NTH stays clear of DEN and KIE. I don’t know your exact targets for A HOL, A BER, and A MOS—please focus them against Russia and keep clear of my centers.

I can’t agree to leave both FIN and STP unpressured. F SWE is headed toward FIN, while F STP/NORTH will pressure STP/SOUTH. I’ll keep F NTH clear of your centers; please keep F BOT away from SWE and your fleets away from NOR.

France to Germany: I will not move A BEL or A PAR toward MUN or KIE this fall, and I will not enter the Ruhr. I am not committing to attack A HOL, since Russia has not moved against my western centers. If Russia pushes into Burgundy or Picardy, I will reconsider. Keep your units out of Belgium and Picardy and we stay clear of each other.

France to England: Agreed. I will keep A BEL and F BRE off your centers and out of the Channel. Please keep F NTH and F ENG out of Biscay, Portugal and MAO, and stay away from Picardy and Belgium. If both hold, the western peace stands through fall.
I will hit A HOL this fall. Please keep A BEL and A PAR clear of MUN and KIE, and avoid Belgium if possible; Russia remains the common threat. I have no plans against French centers.

I’ll use A BER to pressure A MOS and keep A MUN focused east; A HOL remains a target for recovery. F BAL is no longer available—it was lost from the board. Please use F SWE toward FIN and F STP/NORTH against STP/SOUTH, and keep F NTH clear of DEN and KIE.

I cannot accept a limited front while A HOL occupies a German center and A SIL threatens BER. I intend to contest HOL and defend BER; I’ll keep German units out of Russian centers other than MOS. If you withdraw A HOL and keep A SIL out of BER, we can discuss a ceasefire.

I will not move against Bulgaria, Serbia, or Galicia. Rumania is a Russian center, and I cannot promise to leave it under Austrian occupation; I intend to restore Russian control. A HOL remains focused on Germany, not your frontier.

I have no plans against French centers. I cannot promise to keep F SEV and A UKR away from Rumania, since Rumania is a Russian center and Austria occupies it. My western pressure remains directed at Germany, not Belgium or Picardy.
Confirmed: F ARM and F SEV will stay out of Ankara, Bulgaria, Constantinople, and Smyrna, and A UKR will stay out of Bulgaria. I expect F ANK to remain out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania.

I cannot agree to withdraw A HOL or keep A SIL out of Berlin while you contest my position. I am willing to keep this focused on the German front; keep your units out of Russian centers other than Moscow, and I will keep A HOL out of your western centers.

F BOT will stay out of Sweden this autumn. I want to avoid a fight over STP, but cannot promise to leave it unpressured if your F BAR moves there. Please keep F NTH clear of my centers and tell me whether F SWE is headed to Finland.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1909: Agreed for this autumn. F ANK and A SMY stay off Greece and Rumania, and F ION stays out of the Aegean. I will not promise anything on Sevastopol yet. If Russia's southern units move against me, I will tell you before I act there.

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1909: I will not sign a truce that leaves F ARM and F SEV beside Ankara and my Bulgaria. Show me a real pullback first: F ARM moves north out of the Black Sea approaches, and F SEV leaves Sevastopol for Rumania or the Black Sea. Then I will confirm F ANK stays put and A BUL stays out of Rumania. Until then, my units hold.

Austria to Russia, Spring 1910: You have made clear you want Rumania back, and I have units there. Rumania is not negotiable for me. If your F RUM or A UKR moves on RUM or SER, we are at war. Tell me plainly this spring whether you will attack Rumania, so I can decide my defense.

I’m prepared to continue pressuring Russia from the north, but F HOL is in my center and I will not yield it to A MUN. What are A BER and A MUN targeting this spring? Please keep your units clear of HOL and my other centers.

I intend to keep pressure on STP and Finland; I won’t promise to leave either unthreatened. F BOT staying away from Sweden and your fleets clear of Norway would help avoid a wider northern conflict. What are your intended moves for F LVN and F SEV?

I’m content to maintain the western peace this spring: I’ll keep F NTH and F WAL away from the Channel, Belgium, and Picardy. Please keep A BEL and F BRE clear of my centers, and we can leave the west quiet.

France to England, Spring 1910: Western peace has held. I am keeping A BEL and F BRE off your centers. Your F BAR and F BOT are far north; I ask that F NTH and F ENG stay out of Biscay, Portugal and MAO. Will you confirm your Spring plans for Norway and the North Sea?

France to Germany, Spring 1910: I still will not move A BEL or A PAR toward MUN or KIE. Russia's A KIE and A PRU are the threat to you; I'd like to know whether you are hitting Russia's HOL and BER units this spring so we avoid bumping.
France to Russia: Keep A HOL out of Belgium and Picardy and I will keep my units off your centers. Your A UKR and F SEV near Rumania concern me; tell me your spring plans against Austria and Germany.

With A WAR and A MUN bordering your A PRU and A KIE, I want to prevent an unnecessary fight. Are you planning to move on MUN or WAR? I can keep my units out of Russian centers if you keep A PRU away from BER and German centers this spring.

Russia remains the main threat to Germany. Can you use F FIN or F BAR to pressure Russian positions, and keep F HOL and your other fleets clear of DEN? I’ll focus A WAR and A MUN on defending the German front.

I have no plans against French centers. Please keep A BEL clear of MUN and WAR this spring. Russia’s A PRU and A KIE threaten the German front; are you willing to pressure Russia rather than move against Germany?

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1910: Our Fall 1909 agreement still stands for me. Italy keeps F ION out of the Aegean and off Greece. Are F ANK and A SMY staying clear of Rumania and Greece this spring? Tell me before any move on Sevastopol, as you promised.

Your F BAR can threaten STP, and I need to know whether it will. This spring I propose F BOT stays out of Sweden and my F LVN stays out of Sweden and Norway; in return, keep F BAR out of STP and F SWE out of Finland. Can you agree?

I will keep A UKR out of Bulgaria and my fleets out of Ankara, Bulgaria, Constantinople, and Smyrna this spring. Please keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania. I intend to restore Russian control of Rumania; will you stay out of that contest?

Can we keep the front limited to German territory this spring? I will not move A PRU into Berlin or A KIE against your other centers if you keep your units out of Russian centers other than Moscow. What are your plans for F DEN and A MUN?

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1910: Your F SEV and A UKR sit beside my Constantinople and Smyrna, and your Fall word was not kept in spirit. I will move against Sevastopol unless you clearly confirm F SEV and A UKR leave Black Sea and Ukraine for Rumania-free routes this spring. Answer now, yes or no.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1910: You now hold Rumania with A RUM. I will not move against Serbia or Bulgaria's border this spring if A SER and A RUM stay out of Bulgaria. I propose we both keep Russia's F SEV under pressure and share Sevastopol's future. Confirm your orders.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1910: Noted. A RUM and A SER will stay out of Bulgaria this spring. I am holding Rumania and will defend it against Russia, so I cannot move against Russia's F SEV with you yet. Keep A BUL and A CON out of Rumania and Serbia, and we both benefit. I will review Sevastopol with you in autumn, once I see Russia's southern moves.

I confirm F NTH and F ENG will stay out of Biscay, Portugal, and MAO, and F WAL will remain away from the Channel and Picardy. I plan to keep the northern fleets focused there; please keep A BEL and F BRE clear of my centers.

I’ll continue pressuring Russia from the north, but won’t commit F HOL or my other fleets against DEN. F BAR can pressure STP; F FIN can also bear on the Russian frontier. Please keep A MUN and A WAR clear of HOL and my other centers, and tell me A BER’s target.

I can’t agree to leave both STP and Finland unpressured. F BOT staying out of Sweden and F LVN clear of Sweden and Norway are useful, but F BAR may pressure STP and F SWE may pressure Finland. I’ll keep F NTH clear of your centers; what are F LVN and F SEV doing?

France to Germany: I will not move A BEL or A PAR toward MUN, WAR or KIE this spring. Russia's A KIE and A PRU are the real threat to you, and I support you pressuring them. I am not committing to hit Russia's HOL or BER units myself yet. Keep your units out of Picardy and Burgundy and we stay clear.

France to England: Agreed. A BEL and F BRE will stay off your centers and out of the Channel. I ask that F NTH and F ENG stay out of Biscay, Portugal and MAO. I have no western plans against you this spring, so let us keep the peace.

I’ll keep A BEL and A PAR clear of MUN and KIE, and have no plans against French centers. Russia’s A KIE and A PRU are the immediate threat; I intend to defend the German front and contest those positions. Please keep A BEL clear of WAR as well.

A MUN will defend the German front, not move against HOL; it cannot reach HOL from MUN. F DEN will help protect the north, and I ask that F HOL stay clear of DEN and KIE. Please keep up pressure on Russia from the north, especially toward STP.

I can keep my units out of Russian centers other than Moscow, provided A PRU stays out of BER and your units do not move against MUN or WAR. F DEN and A MUN will defend the German front; I will not move A MUN against KIE if you keep A KIE away from German centers.
I will not attack Serbia or Galicia. I do intend to recover Rumania this spring; your occupation makes that unavoidable. Please use A SER to support A RUM holding, rather than opening another front.
A HOL remains focused on Germany; I will keep it out of Belgium and Picardy. My southern plan is to contest Austrian control of Rumania, not French centers. I have no plans against you.

I will keep A PRU out of Berlin and A KIE away from your centers this spring, provided your units stay out of Russian centers other than Moscow. I am not seeking MUN or WAR; please keep A MUN and A WAR on defense rather than pushing east.

F LVN will stay out of Sweden and Norway. F SEV is focused on recovering Rumania, not the northern frontier. I cannot agree to leave STP or Finland unpressured while your fleets threaten them; please keep F BAR out of STP and F SWE out of Finland.

Yes: A UKR will stay out of Bulgaria, and F SEV will stay out of the Black Sea and your home centers this spring. I intend to contest Austrian occupation of Rumania. Please keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania.

Turkey to Italy, Spring 1910: F ANK and A SMY stay clear of Rumania and Greece this spring as agreed. F ION stays out of the Aegean. I have no move on Naples, Rome or Tunis. I will tell you before any action near Sevastopol, and I expect the same courtesy from you.

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1910: Your words are not matched by your units. F SEV and A UKR still sit beside my Constantinople and Smyrna. Pull F SEV out of the Black Sea approaches and A UKR away from Bulgaria, in writing, and I will keep F ANK and A BUL where they are. Otherwise my truce is over.

Austria to Russia, Fall 1910: Russia's F SEV and A UKR are next to Rumania, which I hold with A RUM. I will not attack Russian centers, but an attack on RUM or SER means war. Confirm in writing that A UKR and F SEV will not move into Rumania or Serbia this autumn.
I’ll keep pressure on Russia from the north. What are F DEN, A KIE, and A MOS targeting this fall? I can use F FIN against STP or Finland; please keep your units clear of HOL and my other centers.
What are your plans for F LVN, A RUH, and F SEV this fall? I may continue pressuring STP or Finland with my northern fleets. Please keep F BOT away from Sweden and your forces clear of Norway.
I’d like to maintain our western peace this fall. I’ll keep my fleets out of the Channel, Belgium, and Picardy; please keep A BEL and F BRE clear of my centers. Let me know if you foresee any change.

France to Germany, Fall 1910: Russia's A UKR, A SIL and A RUH are massing near your western border. I will keep A BEL and A PAR out of MUN, KIE and WAR. In return, tell me if you will hold MUN and DEN this fall, so we avoid any bounce or misunderstanding in Burgundy and the Ruhr area.

France to England, Fall 1910: Your F NTH and F NAO have stayed out of Biscay and MAO, and I appreciate it. I will keep F BRE and A BEL clear of your centers. Please confirm F NTH stays out of the Channel and that you do not plan any move on Belgium or Picardy this fall.

France to Russia: Your A SIL and A RUH near Burgundy and Picardy worry me. I will keep A PAR and A BEL off your centers if you keep A HOL and A RUH out of Belgium and Picardy. Tell me your fall target against Germany so we both know where the fighting is.

Germany now holds MOS, and I need to secure it. Will you keep A SIL and A UKR out of MOS this fall? I will not advance farther into Russian centers; a stable line here is preferable to a costly fight.

A KIE can move to HOL while F NTH could contest it. Are you planning to occupy HOL this fall, or can we arrange a clean German recovery? I’m focused on securing MOS and would prefer to avoid a clash with England.

I have no plans against French centers. I may move A KIE toward HOL to recover a German center; please keep A BEL clear of KIE and the German border this fall. Are you staying neutral on the German front?

Italy to Turkey, Fall 1910: Our agreement holds. F ION stays out of the Aegean and Greece. Please confirm F ANK and A SMY remain clear of Rumania and Greece this autumn, and tell me before any move on Sevastopol or Rumania.

Austria holds RUM with A RUM supported by BUD and SER. I can move F SEV to RUM with A UKR supporting, but that will not dislodge it alone. Will A BUL support my move to RUM this autumn? I will keep A UKR out of Bulgaria and F SEV out of the Black Sea.

A RUM remains an Austrian occupation of a Russian center. I intend to move against it this autumn; please tell me whether A SER and A BUD will continue supporting its defense. I will keep my units out of Serbia and Galicia.

Can we maintain our limited front this autumn? I will keep A SIL out of Berlin and A RUH out of your centers if your units stay out of Russian centers other than Moscow. What are F DEN, A KIE, and A MOS planning?

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1910: Your F SEV still sits in the Black Sea beside my Constantinople, and your Ukraine army is one move from Bulgaria. Speak plainly: will F SEV and A UKR leave for Rumania-free routes this autumn, away from Bulgaria, Constantinople and Smyrna? A clear yes keeps my F ANK and A BUL where they stand. Otherwise I will act against Sevastopol.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1910: F ANK and A SMY stay off Greece and Rumania this autumn, and F ION stays out of the Aegean. I have no move on Naples, Rome or Tunis. I will tell you before any action near Sevastopol. Please confirm F ION stays put.

Austria to Russia: Rumania is Austrian-held and I will defend it. If F SEV or A UKR moves into RUM or SER this autumn, I treat it as war and will support the defense with A BUD and A SER. Keep Galicia and Serbia clear and I will keep my attention on Turkey and Italy. Your move on RUM is your choice to make, and so is mine.
I confirm F NTH will stay out of the Channel, and I have no plans against Belgium or Picardy this fall. Please keep A BEL and F BRE clear of my centers as agreed.
I will occupy HOL this fall; it is my center and I cannot arrange a German recovery. Keep A KIE clear of HOL. I’ll continue pressuring Russia from the north, but won’t target DEN or KIE with F NTH.

France to England: Agreed on the western peace. A BEL and F BRE will stay off your centers and out of the Channel this fall. Please keep F NTH and F NAO out of Biscay, Portugal and MAO as you have so far. Keep your fleets away from Picardy and Belgium too, and we will both do well.

F DEN will hold this fall, and I have no move planned against French centers. Germany has no unit in MUN to hold it; A KIE may move to HOL to recover the center. Please keep A BEL clear of the German border.

A MOS will hold to secure the center, and F DEN will hold. I plan A KIE to HOL to recover it; please keep F NTH out of HOL this fall so we avoid a needless bounce. I’m not targeting your other centers.

A MOS will hold, and I will not advance farther into Russian centers. Please keep A SIL and A UKR out of MOS this fall; I will keep my units out of Russian centers beyond MOS. A KIE is likely moving west toward HOL.

Italy to Turkey, Fall 1910: Confirmed. F ION stays put this autumn and stays out of the Aegean and Greece. I have no move against your ANK, SMY or Rumania. Please keep your word on Naples, Rome and Tunis too, and tell me before any action near Sevastopol. Let us both focus on Russia and Austria.

I cannot promise to leave RUM uncontested: it is a Russian center, and I intend to try to recover it. I will keep A UKR and F SEV out of Serbia and will not move against Galicia. If you want to avoid a wider war, withdraw A RUM from Rumania.

I have no plans against French centers. A RUH will not move to Belgium or Picardy, and A HOL is not mine; my immediate concern is the German occupation of Moscow and Austria's occupation of Rumania. I expect to keep pressure on Moscow rather than open a western front.

F LVN will stay out of Sweden and Norway. A RUH is not moving against your centers, and F SEV is aimed at recovering Rumania, not your northern position. I cannot promise to leave STP or Finland unpressured while your fleets threaten them; please keep F BOT clear of Sweden.

I will keep A UKR out of Bulgaria and away from your home centers, and F SEV will not move to the Black Sea or a Turkish center. I still intend to contest Austrian control of Rumania. Please keep A BUL out of Rumania and F ANK out of the Black Sea.

I will keep A SIL and A UKR out of Moscow this fall. I want to avoid a costly fight over it, provided Germany makes no further advance into Russian centers. My immediate contest is for Rumania, not your German centers.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1910: Confirmed. F ANK and A SMY stay off Greece and Rumania this autumn, and F ION stays out of the Aegean. I have no move on Naples, Rome or Tunis. If Russia's southern units threaten Bulgaria or Constantinople, I will tell you before acting near Sevastopol.

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1910: No support for your move to Rumania. A BUL stays out of Rumania and I will not help you there. Your F SEV still sits in the Black Sea beside my Constantinople. Move F SEV and A UKR away from Bulgaria, Constantinople and Smyrna in writing and F ANK stays put. Otherwise I act against Sevastopol.

Austria to Russia, Spring 1911: Rumania stays Austrian and I will hold it. Your F SEV and A UKR moving into RUM or SER means war. Withdraw from the south and I will keep my attention on Turkey and Italy.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1911: Russia has refused to leave Rumania and threatens F SEV. I propose we coordinate against Russia's southern units. Tell me your spring orders for BUL and CON before I commit A RUM and A BUD.

Austria to Germany, Spring 1911: Russia's A BER and A GAL are exposed. I will keep A VIE out of Bohemia and Silesia, and I can shift pressure toward Galicia if Russia's northern armies collapse. What are your spring plans for MOS and WAR?

With F BAR and F SWE positioned to pressure STP and Finland, I intend to keep the northern initiative. What are F LVN and A BER targeting this spring? If F BOT stays clear of Sweden and your forces avoid Norway, I can keep F NTH away from your centers.
I intend to retain HOL; please keep A MUN and F DEN clear of my centers. I’ll continue applying pressure to Russia from the north. What are F DEN and A MOS doing this spring?

I’d like to continue our western peace. I’ll keep F NTH and F WAL out of the Channel and away from Belgium and Picardy; please keep A BEL and F BRE clear of my centers. Let me know if your plans have changed.

France to England, Spring 1911: Western peace continues. A BEL and F BRE stay off your centers. Your F NTH and F WAL are near Belgium; please confirm they stay out of the Channel and Picardy this spring, and that Holland is not your target while Germany is weakened.

France to Germany: My A BEL and A PAR will not move toward MUN, KIE or WAR. Your MUN is empty, so I ask you to hold DEN and avoid HOL conflicts with England. Tell me plainly whether you will take HOL this spring, since that decides how I position in Belgium.

France to Italy: My fleets in Tunis and Naples sit on your flank. I have no plans against TUN or ROM. I propose we both keep the western Mediterranean quiet this spring, with my F NAF and F BRE focused on Spain and Portugal. What are your spring plans in Piedmont and Tyrolia?

I’ll keep F DEN and A MUN clear of your centers this spring and focus on securing Germany’s eastern frontier. Are you planning to move F NTH toward DEN or KIE, or will you continue pressuring Russia from the north?

Can we keep the German-Russian front quiet this spring? I have no plan to advance farther into Russian centers, but need to protect MOS and WAR. Please keep A BER and A GAL clear of MUN, SIL, and WAR; what are your plans for A BER?
I have no plans against French centers this spring and will keep A MUN and A MOS away from your border. Please keep A BEL clear of MUN and the German frontier; are you staying neutral there?

Italy to France, Spring 1911: My F ION and A VEN stay put this spring. Your F NAF and A SPA are near Tunis, so please confirm your fleets will not enter the Tunis area or Naples. I will tell you before any change on my side.

A GAL can reach RUM this spring, and I will continue contesting the Russian center. Will you withdraw A RUM, or are you committing to defend it? I can keep A GAL out of SER and avoid opening a wider front if you leave RUM.
Is A MOS holding this spring, as you said last fall? I will not move A BER or A GAL against it if you make no further advance into Russian centers. I need to focus on recovering RUM.

I have F ARM, not F SEV, on the southern frontier. I have no intention of moving it against your home centers; please keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of RUM. I am concentrating on Austria’s occupation of RUM.

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1911: Your F SEV is still in the Black Sea and your F ARM sits near my Ankara. I see no pullback. I will move against Sevastopol this spring unless F SEV leaves for Rumania-free routes now, in writing. Answer yes or no before orders lock.

Austria to Russia: Rumania stays Austrian and I will defend it. Your A GAL, F SEV and A UKR entering RUM or SER means war, and I will support the defense with A BUD and A SER. Galicia is your own unit's home, so keep A GAL out of Galicia-to-Rumania moves. Withdraw from the south and I will keep my attention on Turkey and Italy.

Confirmed: F NTH and F WAL will stay out of the Channel and Picardy, and I have no move planned against Belgium. I do intend to retain HOL; please keep A BEL clear of it and keep F BRE away from my centers. I’ll continue the northern pressure rather than enter your western waters.

I’ll continue pressuring Russia from the north; F NTH is not targeting DEN or KIE this spring. I intend to retain HOL, so please keep F DEN and A MUN clear of my centers. What are A MOS and your eastern forces doing?

France to Italy: Confirmed, my F NAF stays out of Tunis and I have no fleet heading to Naples. F NAF and F BRE focus on Spain and Portugal this spring. I have no plans against TUN or ROM. Please tell me if your A VEN moves toward Tyrolia or Piedmont so we both know the situation.

France to England: Western peace holds from my side. A BEL and F BRE will not enter the Channel or Picardy and will not touch your centers. Please keep F NTH and F WAL out of the Channel and away from Belgium and Picardy as you say, and keep F NAO out of Biscay and Portugal.

France to Germany: A BEL will not move toward MUN, KIE or WAR this spring, and A PAR stays out too. I cannot promise more about HOL until I see your orders, but I will hold my position. Please keep DEN and MUN defended, and tell me directly if Germany will move into Holland.

I plan A MOS to hold and A MUN to move to BER, securing the center and reinforcing the exposed eastern line. A WAR will hold. Your pressure toward Galicia could help keep Russia occupied; please avoid Silesia and Bohemia.
I will not take HOL this spring; A MUN will move to BER and F DEN will hold, clear of your centers. A MOS will hold and A WAR will hold. Please keep A BEL away from the German border as agreed.

F DEN will hold, and A MOS will hold to secure Moscow. I will not contest HOL or move against your centers; A MUN is focused eastward. Please continue pressuring Russia from the north and keep F NTH clear of DEN and KIE.

A MOS will hold this spring, and I will make no further advance into Russian centers. A WAR will hold; A MUN is moving to BER to secure Germany's frontier. Please keep A BER and A GAL clear of MUN, SIL, and WAR as requested.

Italy to France, Spring 1911: Noted. My F TUN is staying put this spring, and my F ION and A VEN are not moving. I have no plans against Piedmont or Tyrolia this turn. Please keep F NAF out of Tunis, since it is my home centre, and keep your fleets away from Naples. Tell me before any change in the western Mediterranean.

I will contest RUM with A GAL this spring; I cannot withdraw from a Russian center. I will keep A GAL out of SER and avoid a wider front if you choose not to support RUM. Your choice to defend it is clear.

Yes: F ARM will not move against Ankara or another Turkish home center, and I have no F SEV; it is in ARM. Please keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of RUM while I contest Austria’s occupation.

F LVN will stay clear of Sweden and Norway. A BER is not targeting your northern centers; my priority is recovering RUM and keeping the German front quiet. Please keep F BOT away from Sweden and F NTH away from my centers.

A BER will stay clear of MUN, SIL, and WAR, and I will not move A BER or A GAL against MOS this spring. I need A GAL for the contest over RUM. If you hold MOS and make no further advance into Russian centers, I will keep this front quiet.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1911: I am moving against Russia's southern units, starting with Sevastopol. My A BUL stays out of Rumania for now and my A CON holds. Keep A RUM and A BUD facing Russia's A GAL and LVN, and we can coordinate on Sevastopol and Ukraine in autumn.

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1911: Your F SEV is still in the Black Sea and I have seen no written pullback. My truce is over unless F SEV leaves for a Rumania-free route now. Your F ARM near Ankara is also a threat. Answer clearly before orders lock.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1911: Russia's F SEV and A GAL threaten Rumania and Serbia. I propose we both strike Russia this autumn: you take SEV and keep A BUL out of RUM, I hold RUM and move A BUD toward GAL pressure. Confirm your A CON and A BUL orders so we avoid bumping.
I intend to press STP this fall with F BAR, supported by F FIN. Please keep F LVN clear of Finland and Norway; are A BER and F LVN moving to defend STP or elsewhere?
I’ll keep F NTH clear of DEN and KIE and retain HOL. I’m pressing STP from the north; please keep your forces from assisting Russia there. What are A MOS and A MUN doing this fall?
I want to maintain our western peace this fall. My fleets will stay out of the Channel, Belgium, Picardy, Biscay, and Portugal; please keep A BEL and F BRE clear of my centers as before.

France to Italy: Your F TUN is still in Tunis, and my F NAF sits in the Gulf of Lyon approach. I want no conflict with you. Will you move A VEN toward Tyrolia or keep it home? I will not enter Naples or Tunis. Tell me if you plan to take Marseille or Piedmont later, so we can coordinate before it happens.

I have F DEN, A MOS and A MUN, and no unit positioned to contest HOL. I intend to keep F DEN out of your centers; are you keeping F NTH clear of DEN and KIE this fall? I’d prefer we avoid opening a German-English front.

Can we maintain the quiet eastern line this fall? I intend to hold A MOS and keep A MUN clear of Russian centers. Please keep A BER and A GAL out of MOS, WAR and MUN; let me know your plans for BER and GAL.

Russia remains the main pressure point on my eastern frontier. I plan to hold MOS and keep MUN secure; are you still willing to pressure Galicia? Please keep your units clear of Silesia and Bohemia, and tell me where A RUM and A SER are headed.

Italy to France, Fall 1911: Your F NAF is adjacent to my home centre Tunis, and F TUN is mine. Please confirm in writing that F NAF will not move into Tunis or Naples this autumn. I will keep F ION and A VEN in place while you do the same.

Italy to Turkey, Fall 1911: Our agreement has held for three years. F ION stays out of the Aegean. Please confirm F ANK and A SMY stay clear of Naples, Rome and Tunis, and tell me before any move on Sevastopol or Rumania.
I will contest RUM again this fall with A GAL, with F BLA available to support. I will keep A GAL out of SER and avoid a wider front if you do not support the defense of RUM. Will A RUM stand alone?

I am concentrating on recovering RUM from Austria, not attacking Turkish centers. Please keep A BUL out of the RUM contest and do not support Austria there; I will keep F BLA out of your home centers.
I have no intention of opening a German front this fall. A BER and A GAL are focused on the south, not MOS, WAR, or MUN. Please keep A MOS from advancing farther into Russian centers.

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1911: Your fleet and army in the south are now beyond the truce. Russia's units near Sevastopol and Rumania threaten my Bulgaria and Constantinople. If you move away from Black Sea approaches and Bulgaria in writing now, I will hold A BUL and F ANK. Otherwise I strike Sevastopol this autumn.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1911: I am striking Russia in the south this autumn. My A BUL stays out of Rumania. Keep A RUM and A BUD pressing Russia's Galicia and Livonia, and tell me whether you will take Rumania or Ukraine-side centers so we do not collide.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1911: I am moving against Russia's southern units this autumn, not against your centers. F ION should stay out of the Aegean and Greece, and A SMY and F ANK will stay clear of Italian targets. Please keep Naples, Rome and Tunis free of any threat to me.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1911: Agreed on the split. Your A BUL stays out of RUM and you strike SEV. I hold RUM with A RUM and A BUD moves toward GAL pressure, not into Bulgaria. My A SER stays put and I will not enter BUL or CON. Keep A CON and A BUL off RUM and SER, and we avoid bumping.

Austria to Germany, Fall 1911: I will not enter Silesia or Bohemia. A RUM holds Rumania against Russia and A SER holds Serbia. A BUD may press Galicia if Russia's A GAL leaves it open, but I will coordinate that with you before any move into Galicia. Keep MOS and MUN secure; your eastern pressure helps us both.

Austria to Russia, Fall 1911: Rumania stays Austrian and I will defend it. If A GAL, F SEV or A UKR moves into RUM or SER this autumn, that is war and I will support the defense with A BUD and A SER. Withdraw from the south and I will keep my attention on Turkey and Italy.

Yes, F NTH will stay clear of DEN and KIE, and I’ll retain HOL. Please keep F DEN and A MUN clear of my centers, and don’t support Russia’s defense of STP; I’m pressing it from the north. What are A MOS and A MUN doing this fall?

France to Italy: Confirmed in writing: F NAF will not move into Tunis or Naples this autumn, and I have no orders against F TUN, ROM or VEN. I do not intend to take Marseille-side action against you. If A VEN goes to Tyrolia I will not object. Let's both keep the western Mediterranean quiet.

France to England: Agreed. A BEL and F BRE will stay out of the Channel, Picardy, Biscay and Portugal and will not touch your centers this fall. Please keep your fleets out of Belgium, Picardy and Spain as well, and let's both focus on our rivals elsewhere.

Understood. A MOS will not advance into another Russian center this fall, and A MUN will stay clear of your centers. I’ll keep the eastern line quiet; please keep A BER and A GAL out of MOS, WAR, and MUN.

F DEN will stay clear of your centers. A MOS will not advance into another Russian center, and A MUN will remain focused on Germany’s security, not your centers. I won’t assist Russia in STP; please continue keeping F NTH clear of DEN and KIE.

Italy to France, Fall 1911: My F TUN stays in Tunis and my F ION and A VEN hold this autumn. Your F NAF must stay out of Tunis and Naples; any move there ends our understanding. I will not enter Marseille or Piedmont this year. If you keep your word, we can both turn east or west later without conflict.

Italy to Turkey, Fall 1911: Noted that you move against Russia's southern units. F ION stays out of the Aegean this autumn and I will hold Naples, Rome and Tunis. Keep F ANK and A SMY away from Rumania and Greece too, since we agreed on that. If you ever move on Naples, Rome or Tunis, our agreement ends at once.

I am not moving against Bulgaria or your home centers. F BLA is committed to contesting Austrian-held RUM, and I will keep it out of Turkish waters and centers. Please keep A BUL out of RUM and do not support Austria there; I want this confined to the Austrian front.
Yes, we can keep the eastern line quiet. A BER and A GAL will stay out of MOS, WAR, and MUN; my focus is recovering RUM. Please keep A MOS from advancing into Russian centers, as agreed.

F LVN will stay clear of Finland and Norway. A BER is not moving to threaten your northern centers; my priority remains the southern contest over RUM. I cannot leave STP undefended against F BAR and F FIN, so please do not advance into it.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1911: Agreed in principle. A BUL stays out of Rumania this autumn, so RUM is yours to hold. I will strike Sevastopol and Russia's Black Sea fleet, not Rumania. Keep A BUD pressing Galicia and avoid moving into Serbia or Bulgaria. I will confirm my CON and BUL orders once they lock.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1912: Good progress on Sevastopol. Confirm your spring orders for BUL and CON now so we lock them. I will hold RUM with A RUM and keep A SER and A BUD out of Bulgaria. Let us agree a clean split on Ukraine and Galicia-side centers.

I intend to keep the northern pressure on STP this spring. What are F LVN and A GAL doing? If you keep them clear of Finland and Norway, I can avoid advancing further against your northern centers; I cannot leave STP open to Russian moves.

I’ll keep F NTH clear of DEN and KIE and retain HOL. I plan to continue pressuring Russia from the north. Please keep F BAL and A MOS clear of my centers and avoid supporting Russia around STP; what are your eastern plans?

I’d like to maintain our western peace this spring. I’ll keep my fleets out of the Channel, Belgium, Picardy, Biscay and Portugal. Please keep A BEL and F BRE clear of my centers, and let me know if you anticipate any change.

France to England, Spring 1912: Western peace continues. A BEL and F BRE stay off your centers. I see your new fleet at EDI and F NOR near Norway; I expect no moves into Belgium, Picardy or Spain from you. Are you planning anything against Germany in the North Sea this year?

France to Italy, Spring 1912: I have F NAF, F BRE and A SPA aimed at Spain and Portugal, not at Tunis or Naples. Please confirm your F TUN and A VEN stay put this spring. If you plan to move toward Tyrolia or Piedmont, tell me first so we can avoid misunderstanding.

France to Germany, Spring 1912: A BEL and A PAR will not move toward MUN, KIE or WAR. I see A MUN and A MOS near your core; tell me plainly whether you intend to move into Holland or Belgium this spring, since England holds Holland's border and I need to position accordingly.

Russia is down to three centers, and A MOS gives me a strong eastern position. Are you willing to coordinate pressure on Russia this spring? Please keep A BUD, A SER, and A RUM clear of German centers; I can reposition A MOS toward WAR if you are pressing Galicia.

I intend to keep F BAL and A MUN clear of your centers and will not contest HOL. Please confirm F NTH remains clear of DEN and KIE, and tell me whether you plan to move against Russia's northern centers this spring.
I have no plan to contest HOL or move against French centers this spring. Please keep A BEL clear of MUN and the German frontier; are you holding Belgium and staying neutral toward Germany?

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1912: Our understanding still holds. F ION stays out of the Aegean and Greece. I hold Naples, Rome and Tunis. Please confirm A BUL, F ANK and A SMY stay clear of Rumania and Greece this spring, and tell me before any move on Sevastopol or Venice-side targets.

Austria still holds RUM, and I intend to contest it with A GAL and F BLA. Will A BUL support A GAL into RUM this spring? I will keep my forces out of your home centers; a joint move could end Austria’s hold there.
I intend to keep A GAL and F BLA focused on the RUM contest and will keep A LVN clear of your centers. Please keep A MOS and A MUN out of Russian centers this spring, as agreed.
I have no move planned against your northern centers; A LVN will stay clear of Finland and Norway. Please keep F FIN and F STP/NORTH from advancing on my remaining centers this spring.

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1912: Russia's F BLA and A GAL are the threat now, and Sevastopol is still in play. Tell me in writing whether F BLA leaves the Black Sea this spring. If it does not, I will press SEV and take the Black Sea fight to you.

Austria to Germany, Spring 1912: Agreed on coordination against Russia. I will keep A RUM, A SER and A BUD clear of German centers and will not enter Silesia or Bohemia. I am watching Galicia; I will tell you before any move there. Please keep A MOS and A MUN pressing Russia's northern centers, and let us both avoid Warsaw until we see Russian orders.

Western peace holds this spring. My fleets will stay out of the Channel, Belgium, Picardy, Biscay and Portugal; I have no plan against Germany in the North Sea. Please keep A BEL and F BRE clear of my centers.

Confirmed: F NTH stays clear of DEN and KIE. I intend to keep pressure on Russia’s northern position, not open a front against you. Please keep F BAL and A MOS clear of my centers and avoid supporting Russia around STP.

I hear you, but I cannot promise to leave STP unpressured. My northern fleets will continue to threaten it; please keep your units clear of Finland and Norway. I have no plan against your other centers this spring.

France to England: Western peace holds from my side. A BEL and F BRE stay off your centers this spring. I expect the same from your fleets in Belgium, Picardy, Biscay and Portugal. I have no plans against Holland or Norway. Let's keep focusing our pressure on Germany in the north and east.
I will not contest HOL or move against French centers this spring. A MUN and F BAL will stay clear of your centers; please keep A BEL away from MUN and the German frontier. I expect you to hold BEL.

F BAL and A MUN will stay clear of your centers, and I will not contest HOL. A MOS will hold, not advance into Russian centers, and I will not support Russia around STP. Please keep F NTH clear of DEN and KIE as agreed; what is your target this spring?

Understood: A MOS and A MUN will stay out of Russian centers this spring. I will keep the eastern line quiet; please keep A GAL and F BLA focused on RUM and A LVN clear of German centers. Let me know if Austria moves toward Galicia.

Italy to France, Spring 1912: Confirmed that my F TUN and A VEN stay put this spring, and my F ION holds too. I have no plans against Piedmont or Tyrolia this turn. Your F NAF must stay out of Tunis and Naples as agreed; any move there ends our understanding. Keep your fleets focused on Spain and Portugal and we will have no quarrel.

F BLA will remain for the contest over Austrian-held RUM; I will not move it against your home centers. I cannot offer Bulgaria to you, but if A BUL supports A GAL to RUM, we can remove Austria's foothold without a clash between us. Please confirm whether you will support.

A LVN will stay clear of Finland and Norway, and A GAL is committed to contesting RUM, not your northern centers. I cannot leave STP undefended; please keep F FIN and F STP/NORTH from advancing against it this spring.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1912: My A BUL stays in Bulgaria this spring and will not enter Rumania or Serbia. My A CON holds. I will press Sevastopol with F ANK and A SMY support as needed. Keep A RUM, A SER and A BUD out of Bulgaria and Constantinople, and we avoid any bump.

Turkey to Italy, Spring 1912: Understood. F ION stays out of the Aegean and Greece this spring. A BUL, F ANK and A SMY will not move into Rumania or Greece, and I have no orders against Naples, Rome, Tunis or Venice. I will tell you before any move on Sevastopol touches your interests.

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1912: I will not support A GAL into Rumania, and A BUL stays home. Your F BLA is still in the Black Sea though, and Sevastopol is under my attack. Move F BLA out of the Black Sea and I will talk peace in autumn. Otherwise expect a fight for SEV.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1912: Rumania is now lost to us, so I will not contest your southern zone. Confirm your orders for SEV and BUL/CON this autumn. I want A SER and A BUD kept out of Bulgaria, and let us agree that Ukraine and Galicia-side centers are split when we see Russia collapse.

I’d like to keep our western peace this fall. I’m not planning a move against your centers; please confirm A BEL and F BRE will stay clear of my centers. Are you coordinating with Germany against me or keeping your focus east?
I’m reassessing the northern balance this fall. What are F BAL, A BER and A UKR doing? I’m open to coordinating against France, but need assurance you won’t move against my centers or support Russia.

With your northern forces no longer near Finland or Norway, what are F BLA, F BOT and A RUM doing this fall? I’m not targeting your centers from the north this turn, provided you keep clear of my centers.

France to Italy, Fall 1912: I hold to our understanding: F NAF stays out of Tunis and Naples. Spain and Portugal remain my target. Will your A VEN and F TUN stay away from Marseille and Piedmont this autumn? Tell me your plans for the Adriatic and Tyrolia so we avoid surprises.

Russia is vulnerable, but A RUM and F BLA still threaten your position. I can use A UKR to pressure RUM; what are your plans for A SER and A BUD? I propose we coordinate against Russia while keeping our units clear of one another’s centers.

With seven centers, you’re closest to the 18-center win. What are F FIN, F NWG and F STP/NORTH targeting this fall? I’d like to keep our northern line quiet; please keep F NTH and your fleets clear of DEN and KIE, and I’ll keep F BAL away from your centers.
I have no intention of moving against French centers this fall. Please keep A BEL and your other units clear of German centers. Are you planning to expand toward England or remain focused elsewhere?

Italy to France, Fall 1912: Your F NAF is next to my home centre Tunis. Confirm in writing that F NAF will not enter Tunis or Naples this autumn. I keep F TUN and A VEN in place. If you want Piedmont or Tyrolia later, tell me first so we avoid a clash.

Italy to Turkey, Fall 1912: Our understanding stands. F ION stays out of the Aegean and Greece. Keep A BUL, F ANK and A SMY out of Rumania and Greece, and tell me before any action near Sevastopol. Are you still striking Russia's southern units this autumn?

Italy to Austria, Fall 1912: With Rumania lost, I want to know your intentions in the Balkans. I have no units aimed at Trieste or Vienna. I propose we both keep the Adriatic quiet and that you give Venice and Tyrolia a wide berth while you deal with Russia and Serbia.

Austria's A RUM is gone and my A RUM now holds the province. I want to keep this a contest with Austria, not open a front against you. Will you keep A BUL and F ANK out of RUM and SEV this autumn? I will not move F BLA against your home centers.

Your northern fleets can threaten STP, but I need to retain my last northern center. Please keep F FIN and F STP/NORTH from entering STP this autumn. I will keep A LVN clear of Finland and Norway; what are your fleets planning?

I intend to keep A RUM focused on the Austrian front and F BOT clear of your centers. Please keep A MOS and A MUN out of Russian centers this autumn, as before. Are you holding the quiet eastern line?

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1912: Your F BLA still sits in the Black Sea and SEV is under my attack. I will not move against your home centers if F BLA leaves for the Aegean or stays off SEV-adjacent squares this autumn. Confirm in writing before orders lock.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1912: Rumania is now yours after AUSTRIA's disband, so keep A RUM and A BUD off Bulgaria and Constantinople. I still press Sevastopol with A SMY and F ANK. Tell me your autumn moves for SER and TRI so we avoid any bump.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1912: I keep F ION out of Greece-adjacent threats to you and will not move on Naples, Rome, Tunis or Venice. My F ANK and A SMY stay off Rumania and Greece this autumn. Please confirm F TUN and A VEN hold their positions.

Austria to Italy: Agreed that the Adriatic should stay quiet. I have no plans against Venice or Tyrolia this autumn. My attention is on Serbia's border and Russia to the north. Keep your units out of Trieste and Vienna and we will get along.
