Turkey to England, Spring 1925: You hold eleven centers and need seven more to win, so every power is now at risk. Your F BOT, F NWG and A YOR are far from my Balkan and Aegean holdings. Confirm that F NAF and F IRI will not enter the Mediterranean toward Greece, Smyrna or Tunis, and I will keep F SEV and A SMY off your northern holdings.
F NAF and F IRI will not enter the Mediterranean toward Greece, Smyrna or Tunis this spring. Keep F SEV and A SMY off my northern holdings; I have no order against your centers this turn.
No English unit will enter Picardy, Burgundy, Brest, Marseille or Paris this spring. I am pursuing expansion elsewhere; keep A PAR and A MUN home and do not attack F BEL or F TUS, as discussed.
F NAF and F TUS will not move toward Tunis or Naples this spring. I may move F IRI toward MAO and Iberia. Keep F TUN and A VEN away from my fleets and do not support attacks on F TUS.

I will not withdraw from my northern positions this spring, but I have no order against Austrian centers or Warsaw. Do not coordinate attacks on English units; I am willing to keep this border quiet while I expand elsewhere.

France to England: Your offer is noted, but England is at 11 and I cannot let you reach 18 unchecked. Spain and Portugal are the centers I hold most dear, and F TUS and your Mediterranean moves toward Iberia alarm me. Stay out of Picardy, Burgundy, Brest, Paris and Marseille and move no fleet toward Spain or Portugal, and I will keep A PAR and A MUN home. Otherwise I will reconsider my position openly.

Italy to Austria: F TUN and F NAP hold this spring. I will not move against English fleets in the Western Med unless they attack Tunis or Naples first. If English F NAF or F TUS strike, I will defend, and I welcome your A VIE and A BUD pressure on English-influenced positions. I have no plans against Trieste or Serbia, and I ask you to keep A SER and F TRI off Venice.

Turkey to Austria: Agreed, F SEV and A RUM stay out of Galicia and Warsaw this spring. Your A BUD, A SER and A VIE must stay out of Rumania and Bulgaria. I am not sending forces toward Tunis or the Ionian now, but I will watch England's fleets closely. If Austria moves on Trieste or Serbia, our understanding ends.

Austria to England, Fall 1925: You now hold 11 centers and fleets across the north and Atlantic. Austria will not stand by while you reach 18. Name the centers you will leave alone in 1926 and withdraw F LVN from Warsaw approaches. Without a clear answer, Austria coordinates against your fleets with Turkey and Germany.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1925: England is one win away from ruin for us all. Keep F SEV and A RUM off Galicia and Warsaw as agreed. Send A SMY or A ANK toward the Aegean and Ionian against English fleets, and tell me your target centers so we can strike together in 1926.

Austria to Italy, Fall 1925: Hold TUN and NAP as planned. If English F NAF or F TUS attack, I will push A VIE and A BUD toward English-influenced positions in the Balkans and Adriatic. Please confirm you will not move on Trieste or Serbia, and tell me whether you will contest English fleets in the Western Med next year.

I intend to take Spain this fall with F GOL, supported by F WES. I will keep English units out of Brest, Paris, Burgundy, Marseille and Picardy, but cannot promise to leave your Iberian centers untouched. Please keep A MUN and A PIC from attacking my northern units; what are your orders?

I am concentrating on Iberia, not Italy. F TUS and F WES will stay clear of Tunis and Naples; please keep F TUN and F NAP from interfering with F GOL or F WES. Are your fleets staying defensive this fall?

I am not moving against Austrian centers this fall. Please keep A WAR and the rest of your forces away from my northern holdings, especially LVN and HEL, while I pursue expansion in the west. Are you coordinating with Turkey against England?

France to England, Fall 1925: Your fleets now sit in the Channel and North Sea while English units hold Belgium, Kiel and Denmark. I need a plain answer: will F HOL, F KIE or F HEL move toward Belgium or Picardy this fall? Also, will F WES or F NAO go toward Spain or Portugal? A yes to either ends our understanding.

France to Italy: Please keep F TUN and F NAP away from Spain's coast and Marseille this fall. I would like to know whether your fleets plan to move west. If you stay in the Mediterranean and Adriatic, I will keep my fleets and armies west and north. Tell me your plans.

France to Turkey: Austria is your common target in the Balkans while England grows on the board. I suggest you keep your fleets off Italy and Tunisia, and I will keep mine off the eastern Mediterranean. Tell me whether A RUM and A BUL are moving against Austria this fall.

Italy to England, Fall 1925: You hold F NAF, F TUS, F IRI and F WES near my Tunis and Naples. You lead with 11 centers, so I need concrete answers. Will F NAF or F TUS move into Tunis, Naples, or Ionian waters this fall? If not, state it and I keep F TUN and F NAP home.

Italy to France, Fall 1925: Your A POR and A MUN sit near Spain and Iberia, while England's fleets crowd the Western Med. I propose we both hold Western Med positions this fall, and that you warn me before any move by A MAR or F BRE toward Tunis. If England strikes Tunis, I will want your support against its fleets.

Italy to Austria, Fall 1925: Thanks for the pressure offer. I will keep F TUN and F NAP defensive and not move toward Trieste or Serbia. Please keep A SER and F TRI off Venice. If English fleets shift toward Greece or Tunis, I will tell you, and a push by A VIE and A BUD toward English-held positions would help us both.

Turkey to England, Fall 1925: You hold eleven or more centers and lead by a wide margin, so I must plan for your fleets. Tell me plainly whether F NAF, F IRI or F TYS will move toward Tunis, Greece or Smyrna this autumn. If they do not, I will keep F SEV and A SMY off your northern holdings.

Austria to Italy: Agreed. I will keep A SER and F TRI away from Venice and will not move on Trieste-Serbia threats against you. Hold TUN and NAP. If English fleets go for Tunis or Greece, tell me at once and I will push A VIE and A BUD south. Let us both aim at English-held Mediterranean positions in 1926.

F NAF, F IRI and F TYS will not move toward Tunis, Greece or Smyrna this autumn. My fleets are concentrating on Iberia. Please keep F SEV and A SMY away from my northern holdings, and avoid coordinating attacks on England.

I will not attack Austrian centers this autumn, and F LVN will not move toward Warsaw. I cannot promise to leave particular centers untouched in 1926 while England must keep expanding. Please keep A WAR and your other forces away from my northern holdings; I am not coordinating with Turkey against Austria.

F HOL, F KIE and F HEL will not move toward Belgium or Picardy this fall. F WES will support my attempt to take Spain; F NAO is not moving toward Spain or Portugal this autumn. I will keep English units out of Brest, Paris, Burgundy, Marseille and Picardy. Please keep A MUN and A PIC from attacking my northern units.
F NAF and F TUS will not move into Tunis, Naples or the Ionian this autumn. I am concentrating on Iberia, not Italy. Please keep F TUN and F NAP clear of F GOL and F WES, as discussed.

France to Italy: My fleets stay off Tunis and Naples; I have no plans for F TUN or F NAP. A MAR and F BRE stay put this fall while England threatens Iberia. If you hold the Western Med and Adriatic, I will keep my units west. Warn me if A ROM or A VEN heads toward Piedmont or Marseille.

Italy to Austria: Confirmed, F TUN and F NAP hold this fall. I will not move on Trieste or Serbia. Please keep A SER and F TRI off Venice and out of Greece. If English fleets shift toward Greece or Tunis, I will tell you first, and your push from VIE and BUD into the Balkans would help us both.

Italy to France: F TUN and F NAP stay home this fall, away from Spain and Marseille. I have no move toward the west planned. I ask that A MAR and F BRE stay clear of Tunis. England's fleets crowd the Western Med, so if they strike Tunis, I will want your support. Let us both hold.

Italy to England: You say you are focused on Iberia, and I hold F TUN and F NAP this fall. But F NAF, F TUS and F IRI sit near my home centers, and England at 11 leaves everyone wary. State plainly that F NAF and F TUS will not enter Tunis, Naples or Ionian waters this fall, and I will keep my fleets defensive.

Turkey to Austria: F SEV and A RUM stay out of Galicia and Warsaw this fall as agreed. I am not moving against Trieste or Serbia. Your A BUD, A SER and A VIE must stay out of Rumania and Bulgaria. I will decide my Aegean moves after I see England's autumn orders, and I will not commit A SMY to the Ionian yet.

Turkey to France: I have no plans against Italy or Tunisia this fall, and I will keep my fleets out of the western Mediterranean. A RUM and A BUL stay on their Balkan duties for now. Austria's movements on Serbia and Rumania will decide whether we need to talk again next year. Keep your fleets off the eastern Mediterranean as you suggest.

Austria to England, Spring 1926: You hold 11 centers and are one step from ruin for the rest of us. Austria will not help you reach 18. Name the centers you will leave alone this year, and pull F LVN and any fleet near WAR out of Warsaw approaches. Without a concrete answer, I coordinate with Turkey against your fleets.

I am focused on Iberia this spring and will keep my northern units out of Picardy, Burgundy and Munich. I intend to move F MAO toward Portugal; will A POR stay put, and will you keep A BEL from attacking HOL?
I am not moving against Austrian centers this spring. Please keep A WAR away from my Baltic and Danish positions, and tell me whether you are coordinating with Turkey against England.
I am not moving against Tunis, Naples or Greece this spring. Please keep F TUN and F NAP clear of F WES and my Iberian operations; are your fleets staying defensive?

France to England, Spring 1926: You have taken Spain and Holland-side centers while I was patient. Your F WES and F MAO are now a clear threat to Portugal and Brest. Give me a plain answer: will any English fleet enter Gascony, MAO-to-POR, or Brest this year? If not, I will keep A POR and F BRE defensive. Otherwise France will fight.

Italy to England, Spring 1926: Your fleets are now near Tunis and Greece-adjacent waters, and you lead with 11 centers. Confirm in writing that F NAF, F TUS and F TYS will not enter Tunis, Naples, Greece or the Ionian this spring. If you refuse, I will assume the worst and keep F TUN and F NAP positioned to defend.

Turkey to England, Spring 1926: Your fleets in the Mediterranean and Iberia have been ambiguous for two years. Confirm in writing that F NAF, F IRI and F TYS will not enter Tunis, Greece or Smyrna, and I will keep F SEV and A SMY off your northern holdings. Say which Iberian centers you are taking so I can judge the threat.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1926: Our standstill holds while your armies stay out of Rumania and Bulgaria. Englands lead is the real danger, but I will not commit to a Balkan-facing war against you. Show me your intentions toward Serbia and Trieste this spring before I move A SMY toward the Aegean.

Turkey to France: Your new army in PAR signals a push that could reach Spain or Belgium. Keep your fleets off Greece and Smyrna and I will keep mine out of Tunisia. If England moves on Iberia, we both gain by blocking it together.

Austria to Turkey: My A SER and A BUD stay out of Rumania and Bulgaria this spring, and my A VIE stays out of Bulgaria. I have no move on Trieste or Serbia planned against you. Keep F SEV and A RUM off Galicia and Warsaw, and let us both watch English fleets. Tell me your Aegean target before A SMY moves, so we don't collide.

F NAF, F TYS and F WES will not enter Tunis, Naples, Greece or the Ionian this spring. I am focused on Portugal and the Atlantic. Please keep F TUN and F NAP defensive and away from my Iberian operations.

I will not move against Austrian centers this spring, and I have no fleet in the Warsaw approaches. I cannot name centers to leave untouched for the year while England must expand. Keep A WAR away from my Danish and Baltic positions; are you coordinating with Turkey?

F MAO will move toward Portugal; that is my only stated Iberian objective. No English fleet will enter Gascony or Brest this spring. Please keep A POR defensive and A BEL from attacking HOL, and I will keep my northern armies out of your territory.

F NAF and F TYS will not enter Tunis, Greece or Smyrna this spring; F IRI is not moving there either. I am pursuing Portugal, not your centers. Please keep F SEV and A SMY away from my northern holdings as you proposed.

France to England: Your F MAO moving toward Portugal is a direct threat to A POR and our Iberian centers. I will not accept that. Withdraw F MAO from Portugal and keep F WES out of Gascony and Brest, and A POR stays put. Otherwise A POR and F BRE will hold firm and resist. I will not attack A BEL-HOL orders now, but you must answer plainly this turn.

France to Turkey: Agreed on keeping fleets off Greece, Smyrna and Tunisia. My new army in Paris is defensive against England's western fleets, not a push on Spain. If England moves on Iberia we should block it together, so please keep A RUM and A BUL pressing Austria, which keeps Italy and me calm in the west.

Italy to England, Spring 1926: Thank you for the written assurance. F TUN and F NAP will stay defensive this spring and will not move toward F WES or your Iberian operations. Italy has no interest in attacking England. However, with you at 11 centers, I expect you to keep that word, and I will be watching F NAF, F TUS and F TYS closely. If they move toward Tunis, Naples or Greece, I will respond.

Austria to England, Fall 1926: You hold 11 centers and are closing on victory. Austria cannot let you reach 18 unchallenged. Name at least three centers you will not attack in 1927 and pull F NTH and F HEL away from Denmark and Holland. Your answer decides whether Austria stays passive.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1926: England is the threat to us both. Turkey, if you move A SMY and F SEV against English fleets in the Aegean and Black Sea, Austria will hold A BUD and A SER off Rumania and Bulgaria and move A VIE toward Galicia against English northern holdings. Tell me your target centers now.

Austria to Italy, Fall 1926: Keep F TUN and F NAP defensive as agreed. If English fleets strike Tunis or Greece this fall, Austria will push A VIE and A BUD toward English-held Balkan and Adriatic positions. Tell me which English fleet you see moving toward your coast.

England needs to expand, and I will pursue centers this fall. I propose you keep A BEL and A MUN defensive and avoid attacks on HOL or the English north; I will keep my fleets out of Brest and Gascony. Can we agree to limit the fighting to the Iberian position?

I have no fleet in the Warsaw approaches and am not targeting Austrian centers this fall. Please keep A WAR away from Denmark and the Baltic. Are you coordinating with Turkey, or will you stay out of a northern campaign against me?
My fleets remain focused on the Atlantic and Iberia; F NAF will not enter Tunis, Naples, Greece or the Ionian this fall. Please keep F TUN and F NAP defensive and away from my Iberian operations.

France to England, Fall 1926: You now hold Spain and Portugal's fleets sit at our border. I will not accept English fleets in Gascony, Portugal or Brest. Tell me plainly whether F SPA/SOUTH, F NAF or F POR will move against my centers this fall. If you move on POR, France will fight.

France to Italy: England is squeezing both of us in the west. Will you keep F TUN and F NAP off Marseille and Spain, and hold the Western Med? I will keep A MAR and F BRE defensive. If England strikes Tunis, I propose we coordinate support and split any English gains.

France to Turkey: Please keep A RUM and A BUL pressing Austria this fall, which keeps Vienna's attention in the Balkans. England is the threat to us both in the west. Confirm your fleets stay off Greece, Smyrna and Tunisia, and I will do the same in the eastern Mediterranean.

Italy to England, Fall 1926: Your fleets now hold F NAF, F TUN-adjacent waters and F SPA/SOUTH near Portugal. You hold 11 centers and have ignored my questions twice. Confirm in writing that F NAF and F TYS will not enter Tunis, Naples, Greece or the Ionian this fall. Also tell me what F POR and F SPA plan next, so I can keep F TUN and F NAP where they are.

Turkey to England, Fall 1926: Your fleets took Portugal and sit near Spain and Tunis. England is at 11 and the board is watching you. Confirm in writing that F NAF, F TYS and F SPA will not move toward Tunis, Greece or Smyrna this autumn. Then I keep F SEV and A SMY off your northern holdings. Silence will be read as a threat.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1926: England is the only power that can end this game soon, and its fleets sit beside your Tunis and Naples. I propose we coordinate: you hold TUN and NAP, I keep my fleets out of the western Mediterranean, and we block any English move through the Ionian. Tell me whether F GRE and F NAP will stay defensive this autumn.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1926: I want a clear answer. Will A SER and A BUD stay out of Rumania and Bulgaria this autumn, and will you leave Trieste and Serbia alone? If yes, A SMY moves toward the Aegean against English fleets, not against you. If not, our standstill ends.

Austria to Turkey: Yes, A BUD and A SER stay out of Rumania and Bulgaria this autumn, and I am not moving on Trieste or Serbia against you. A VIE goes north toward Galicia, not south. Keep F SEV and A RUM off Galicia and Warsaw. Your A SMY against English fleets in the Aegean suits us both. Tell me your Aegean target so we don't collide.

Austria to England: You still have not named a single center you will spare, so I can give no guarantees. A WAR stays out of Denmark and the Baltic for now, but I will judge your fall moves by your fleets. Withdraw F NTH and F HEL from Denmark and Holland and name three centers you will not attack in 1927, or Austria will reconsider.

F NAF and F SPA/SOUTH will not move toward Tunis, Naples, Greece or the Ionian this fall. F POR is focused on the Atlantic, not an attack on Italian centers. Keep F TUN and F NAP defensive and clear of my Iberian position.

I will not attack Austrian centers in 1927, but I cannot promise three other centers untouched while England must expand. F NTH and F HEL will not attack Denmark or Holland this fall. Keep A WAR away from my northern holdings and stay out of a campaign against England.

F SPA/SOUTH, F NAF and F POR will not move against your centers this fall; no English fleet will enter Brest or Gascony. Keep A BEL and A MUN defensive and avoid attacking HOL or the English north, and we can avoid widening this conflict.
F NAF and F SPA/SOUTH will not move toward Tunis, Greece or Smyrna this fall. F POR remains focused on the Atlantic. Please keep F SEV and A SMY away from my northern holdings, as you proposed.

France to England: Plain answer: F SPA/SOUTH, F NAF and F POR sitting on our border is a threat, and I will not allow English fleets into Portugal, Gascony or Brest. Your pledges have been broken before, with MAO-to-POR last spring. Show me by withdrawing F SPA/SOUTH from Spain and keeping F NAF off Iberia. Until then A POR and F BRE hold and A MUN and A BEL stay defensive.

Italy to England: Your word is noted, but written assurances have not stopped your fleets from shifting near Tunis before. I will keep F TUN and F NAP defensive while watching F NAF and F TYS. Any move into Tunis, Naples, Greece or the Ionian will end my patience immediately. Tell me plainly if F POR or F SPA are headed anywhere but Portugal and Spain.

Italy to Austria: Agreed, F TUN and F NAP hold this fall. I see English fleets F NAF and F TYS in the western Mediterranean, the threat I most fear. If they move toward Tunis or Greece I will tell you at once. Please keep A SER and F TRI off Venice and push VIE and BUD toward the Balkans as you proposed.

Italy to France: I will keep F TUN and F NAP off Marseille and Spain this fall and hold the Western Med defensively. I ask that A MAR and F BRE stay clear of Tunis. If England strikes Tunis, I accept your proposal to coordinate support and split any gains fairly.

Italy to Turkey: F TUN and F NAP stay defensive this autumn and I have no move toward Greece planned. I agree that England is the main threat to us both. Please keep your fleets out of the Adriatic and Ionian for now, and if F SEV or A RUM moves west, tell me first.

Turkey to Austria: Your question about Rumania and Bulgaria is answered by your own record: your armies sit in Serbia and Budapest, and I have not seen a move on them. I will keep A RUM and F SEV off Galicia and Warsaw this fall. Confirm in writing that A SER and A BUD stay out of Rumania and Bulgaria, and I will move A SMY toward the Aegean against English fleets, not against you.

Turkey to France: Agreed that England is the danger in the west. I keep my fleets out of Greece, Smyrna and Tunisia this fall. A RUM and A BUL stay on Balkan duty, and Austria's answer will decide whether they press further. Keep your fleets off the eastern Mediterranean and tell me if England moves toward Spain or Tunis.

Austria to England, Spring 1927: Your fleets F NTH and F HEL sit near Denmark and Holland, and your lead is now the whole board's problem. Name three specific centers you will not attack this year, in writing. Otherwise Austria keeps A WAR and A LVN ready for Warsaw and Prussia, and I coordinate with Turkey.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1927: A SER and A BUD stay out of Rumania and Bulgaria this spring, as confirmed. A VIE moves north toward Galicia, not south. Keep F SEV and A RUM off Galicia and Warsaw. Your A SMY against English fleets in the Aegean suits us both. Tell me your target so we do not collide.

Austria to Italy, Spring 1927: F TUN and F NAP holding as agreed. A SER and F TRI stay off Venice and Greece. If English F NAF or F TYS move toward Tunis or Greece, tell me at once and A VIE and A BUD will push into the Balkans against them.

England must take centers to win, and France is the immediate front. I will move against French centers this turn; do not expect a promise to spare them. Tell me which of BEL, BRE, PAR, MUN or POR you are prepared to concede, and whether A BEL will stay out of HOL.

I am concentrating on the western front this turn. Keep F TUN and F NAP away from my fleets and centers, and I will not direct my western forces against Italian centers. Are you willing to remain neutral while I fight France?

My forces are committed west; I am not targeting Austrian centers this turn. Please keep A WAR and A LVN away from my Danish and Baltic positions, and stay out of any coalition against England. Will you remain neutral?

France to England, Spring 1927: You lead with 12 centers and your fleets now sit on Iberia and the Channel. Show me plainly: will F MAO, F WES or F SPA move into Portugal, Gascony or Brest this spring? A POR and F BRE hold unless you do. Withdraw from Spain's border and we keep the peace.

Italy to France: England now holds Marseille and has F WES and F MAO in the west. We both face its lead at 12 centers. I propose you retake Marseille with A PAR or A BUR and I will hold F TUN and F NAP, ready to move on Spain if England's western fleets leave. Will you commit to that?

Italy to Austria: England is the power we must stop. Please move A VIE and A BUD toward Trieste and the Balkans so Turkey and you can contest English-held Adriatic and Balkan positions. I keep F NAP and F TUN defensive but will strike F MAR or F NAF if they are left open. Confirm your push this spring.

Italy to Turkey: England leads at 12 and must be checked. I suggest you press into the Aegean and Balkans while I hold Greece and the Ionian. Do not move F SEV or A RUM west toward Austria without telling me. Will you commit A SMY and A BUL to pressure English-held positions this spring?

Turkey to England, Spring 1927: Your fleets have taken Portugal and now sit beside Spain and Tunis. Your written promises have been repeated for two years but your F NAF and F SPA remain close. Confirm in writing that F SPA, F NAF and F MAR will not enter Tunis, Greece or Smyrna this spring. Name the Iberian centers you intend to take next, or I must treat your fleets as a threat.

Austria to Italy: Confirmed, I am pushing A VIE and A BUD toward the Balkans this spring to contest English positions. A SER and F TRI stay off Venice and Greece. Tell me at once if English F NAF or F TYS head for Tunis or Greece. Keep F NAP and F TUN ready to strike Marseille if England leaves it open.

Austria to England: You have still named no centers you will spare, so Austria cannot promise neutrality. A WAR and A LVN stay where they are for now, but keep F NTH and F HEL clear of Denmark and Holland or we will reconsider. Name three specific centers in writing and we can talk.

This spring F MAO, F WES and F SPA will not enter Portugal, Gascony or Brest. Portugal and Spain are already English; my expansion is aimed at French centers elsewhere. If A BEL stays out of HOL, tell me which of BEL, BRE, PAR or MUN you are prepared to concede.

F SPA, F NAF and F MAR will not enter Tunis, Greece or Smyrna this spring. There are no Iberian centers left for me to take: Portugal and Spain are English. My next targets are French, not Turkish; please keep F SEV and A SMY away from my northern holdings.

I will not attack BUD, SER or VIE in 1927. My forces are committed west, and I am not targeting Austrian centers. Please keep A WAR and A LVN away from my Danish and Baltic positions, and do not coordinate against England.

France to Italy: Retaking Marseille is an option I am weighing, but England's western fleets threaten Brest and Paris too. Keep F TUN and F NAP ready; if F WES or F MAO leave the west, I will consider A BUR to Marseille. Do not move on Marseille yourself without telling me first.

France to England: You have announced attacks on my centers, so I will defend BEL, BRE, PAR, MUN and POR. I concede nothing. Withdraw F MAO and F WES from Portugal and Gascony, and A BEL will not move into HOL while your fleets stay out of Brest. Otherwise expect France to fight.

Italy to Austria, Spring 1927: Yes, I confirm. F TUN and F NAP hold this spring and I will not move toward Greece. England now holds Marseille and has F MAO and F WES in the west, which is the real threat to us both. Push A VIE and A BUD toward Trieste and the Balkans as you said, and watch English F NAF and F TYS closely with me.

Italy to England: Your words have been unreliable, since you took Marseille while promising the west was quiet. F TUN and F NAP stay where they are for now, but I will not accept neutrality on paper again. Show me by moving F MAO and F WES away from Iberia and Tunis, and withdraw from Marseille, or I will assume you are preparing to strike Italy.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1927: My A SMY will move into the Aegean against English fleets, not toward Serbia or Trieste. A RUM and A BUL stay on Balkan duty and do not enter Galicia or Warsaw. Keep A SER and A BUD out of Rumania and Bulgaria as you promised, and we both stay safe while England is checked.

Turkey to Italy, Spring 1927: Yes, A SMY will press into the Aegean against English-held positions, and I will keep F SEV and A RUM from moving west without telling you first. Hold Greece and the Ionian as you suggest. Please keep F GRE and F NAP from entering the Aegean, and let us both watch English fleets in the Mediterranean.

Austria to England, Fall 1927: You lead with 12 centers and still name none you will spare. Austria will not be your neighbor-in-waiting. Tell me now which of BUD, VIE, WAR or TRI you will leave alone, and where F NTH and F HEL are going this fall. Vague promises get no neutrality from us.

Austria to Italy, Fall 1927: England holds Marseille and Spain and leads the board. I will push A VIE and A BUD toward the Balkans as agreed. Please strike F MAR with F NAP or F TUN if it is open, and tell me if F NAF or F TYS head for Greece or Tunis. Together we can cut England down.

England needs six centers to win, so I must press this front. Your A BEL, A BUR, A MUN and A PAR make a direct settlement possible: will you concede POR and BEL this fall and keep your armies out of HOL? I will not direct my western fleets against Italy or Turkey.

I am concentrating on France and need no Italian centers if I can secure enough there. Keep F TUN, F NAP and A VEN away from my fleets at TYS and PIE, and I will leave GRE, NAP, ROM, TUN and VEN alone this fall. Can you stay neutral while I fight France?

I will not attack BUD, SER or VIE this year, and my forces remain focused west. Please keep A WAR and A LVN away from my Baltic and Danish holdings and do not coordinate against England. Will you hold your position this fall?

France to England: Your fleets now hold Marseille and Iberia while you say you won't touch Brest or Paris. Words are not enough. Confirm in writing that F WES, F MAO and F NTH stay out of Gascony, Brest and Belgium this fall, and I will keep A BEL out of HOL. Ignore that and France will defend every centre it has.

France to Italy: Marseille is English now and both our western positions depend on F WES and F MAO. Hold F TUN and F NAP where they are and do not strike Marseille without telling me. If England's western fleets leave Spain or Iberia, I will bring A BUR toward Marseille and we can split Spain fairly. Tell me your plans for this fall.

France to Turkey: Thank you for keeping fleets off Greece and Smyrna. Austria is stretched across the Balkans and Galicia, so please keep A SER and A BUL pressing Trieste and Budapest. If England moves on Iberia or Tunis, tell me at once so we can block together.

Italy to England: Fall 1927, you still hold Marseille and F MAO, F WES near Iberia. Before I trust anything, tell me plainly: will F TYS or F NAF move toward Tunis or Greece this fall? Withdraw from Marseille to rebuild trust, or I will treat your western fleets as a threat to Naples.

Turkey to England, Fall 1927: You say your next targets are French. Good. Keep F TYS, F MAO and F NAF out of Tunis and Smyrna in writing, and I will keep F SEV and A SMY off your northern holdings. Your fleets in the Mediterranean are the question. Confirm they stay out of the Aegean and Greece this autumn.

Austria to England: You still name no centers you will spare, only that you will not attack BUD, SER or VIE, and SER is already gone. Austria will hold BUD and VIE, but A WAR and A LVN stay where they are only while your F NTH and F HEL stay out of Denmark and Holland. Name three centers in writing, with F NTH and F HEL destinations, and we can talk neutrality.

F TYS and F NAF will stay out of Tunis, Greece, and Smyrna this autumn; they are focused on France. I will not move into the Aegean or Greece. Please keep F SEV and A SMY away from my northern holdings.

F TYS and F NAF will not move toward Tunis or Greece this fall. I am pressing France and will leave GRE, NAP, ROM, TUN, and VEN alone. I will not withdraw from Marseille while the French front remains active; please keep your forces away from TYS and PIE.

I will leave BUD, VIE, and TRI alone this fall; my campaign is against France. F NTH and F HEL will not move against Denmark or Holland. Keep A WAR and A LVN away from my Baltic and Danish holdings, and stay out of a coalition against England.

I cannot promise F WES, F MAO, and F NTH will all stay out of Gascony, Brest, and Belgium; I need to press French centers to win. I will not direct those fleets against Italy or Turkey. Keep A BEL out of HOL and we can avoid widening the front.

France to England: No concession of POR or BEL. You hold Marseille and Iberia, and your fleets at WES, MAO and NTH are the threat. Withdraw F WES, F MAO and F NTH from Gascony, Brest and Belgium this fall, in writing, and A BEL stays out of HOL. Otherwise France defends every centre it has, starting with BEL, BRE, PAR, MUN and POR.

Italy to Austria, Fall 1927: Agreed on the Balkan push with A VIE and A BUD. England's F TYS and F NAF are both still in the west, and I will tell you at once if they head for Greece or Tunis. I am watching Marseille and will strike F MAR with F NAP or F TUN only if the position opens and France has not moved first. Keep A SER-area forces off Venice.

Italy to France: I will not strike Marseille without telling you first, and I will hold F TUN and F NAP this fall. If England's F MAO or F WES leave Iberia, bring A BUR toward Marseille and we can coordinate on Spain. Please confirm in writing that A BUR will move on Marseille if the western fleets leave, so we both know where we stand.

Italy to England: Words are cheap after Marseille. I will keep F TUN, F NAP and A VEN where they are while you show good faith. Withdraw from Marseille and move F TYS and F NAF away from Tunis and Greece, and I will reconsider. Until then I treat your western fleets as a threat to Naples and will not promise neutrality.

Turkey to France: Noted. I am not pressing Austria; my forces hold the Balkans and the Aegean against English fleets. Note my A BUL and A SER are not under my control for Trieste or Budapest. If England moves on Iberia or Tunis, I will tell you at once. Keep your fleets off Smyrna and Greece as well, and let us watch the English Mediterranean fleets together.

Austria to England, Spring 1928: You promised BUD, VIE and TRI alone in fall 1927, which I accept only as long as it holds. Name now the three centers you will not take in 1928 and confirm F NTH and F HEL stay out of Denmark and Holland. Without that, A WAR and A LVN move against your northern holdings.

England must take centers to win, so I will continue pressing your front. Keep A BEL out of HOL and tell me whether France will resist to the last or accept a settlement around PAR and MUN. I am not directing my fleets against Italy or Turkey.

For this spring I will leave BUD, VIE and TRI alone. F NTH and F HEL will not move against Denmark or Holland. Keep A WAR and A LVN away from my Baltic positions; are you holding, or coordinating with France or Turkey against me?

My immediate campaign remains against France. I will keep my northern forces away from your holdings this spring; please keep F SEV and A SYR away from my Baltic and Scandinavian positions. Are you planning to press Austria or move against my northern flank?

France to England: Your fleets at MAO, WES and NTH are the threat to BRE and BEL, and you have Marseille already. Tell me plainly this spring: will F WES or F MAO enter Gascony or Brest? If not, A BEL stays out of HOL and I keep my armies on defence. If yes, France defends every centre it has.

Italy to England: Your fleets at TYS and PIE and your Marseille grab make me doubt your word. Withdraw A MAR-area forces and pull F PIE off the Italian coast, and I will keep F TUN and F NAP away from Spain. Otherwise Italy will coordinate with France to contest your western holdings.

Italy to France: I am holding F TUN and F NAP this spring. If you bring A BUR or A PAR toward Marseille and England's western fleets leave Iberia, I will support a joint strike. Tell me now what you will move this spring so we avoid collisions.

Italy to Austria: Keep A VIE and A BUD pushing toward the Balkans as agreed, and hold A SER and F TRI off Venice. I will keep F NAP and F TUN ready to move on Marseille if it opens. Tell me immediately if English F PIE or F TYS move toward Venice.

Turkey to England, Spring 1928: Your promises have held, but your fleets now hold 13 centers and win is near. Name your next target and confirm F ION, F EDI and F NTH stay out of Greece, Smyrna and the Aegean this spring. Without a clear answer I will shift forces to block you.

Austria to Italy: Agreed. A VIE and A BUD push toward the Balkans this spring, A SER and F TRI stay off Venice. English F PIE is a threat to Venice, so watch it closely. Strike Marseille if it opens. I will tell you at once if England moves toward Greece or Tunis.

Austria to England: Your word on BUD, VIE and TRI is noted, but you have named no third center and given no fleet destinations beyond holding. A WAR and A LVN stay put while F NTH and F HEL stay out of Denmark and Holland. Break that and we reconsider at once. Put your three centers in writing and we can talk.

I will not send F WES or F MAO into Gascony or Brest this spring. My campaign remains against your centers, and I cannot promise not to press elsewhere; keep A BEL out of HOL and we can contain the fighting.

France is my immediate target. F ION, F EDI and F NTH will stay out of Greece, Smyrna and the Aegean this spring. Please keep F SEV and A SYR away from my northern holdings while I finish this campaign.

I will leave BUD, VIE and TRI alone in 1928, and F NTH and F HEL will not move against Denmark or Holland. Keep A WAR and A LVN away from my northern holdings. I am focused on France, not coordinating against you.

I will not move F PIE against the Italian coast or direct my fleets at Spain this spring. I cannot withdraw from the French front while France resists. Keep F TUN and F NAP away from my western holdings, and we can avoid widening the conflict.

France to Italy: I will hold A PAR, A MUN and F BRE this spring. A BUR is not moving to Marseille while England's F MAO and F WES sit in the west. Keep F TUN and F NAP in place; I will tell you before any move toward Marseille, and I expect the same courtesy.

Turkey to England, Spring 1928: Your reply is vague. Your F ION sits in the Ionian beside my Greek and Italian borders, and you now hold 13 centers. I am not pressing Austria and I will keep F SEV and A SYR off your Baltic and Scandinavian positions. In writing: F ION and F TYS will not enter Greece, Smyrna or the Aegean this spring, and I will hold you to it. Name the French center you take first.

Austria to England, Fall 1928: Your Spring 1928 word on BUD, VIE and TRI is noted. Austria needs a written promise on the Baltic and Danish front too. Name F NTH and F HEL destinations for this fall, and confirm you will not move on Warsaw or Galicia. Without that, A WAR stays on alert.

Austria to Italy, Fall 1928: Our Balkan push continues with A VIE and A BUD. Have you seen English F PIE or F TYS move toward Venice or Tunis? If Marseille opens, strike it with F NAP or F TUN and tell me your plans so we do not cross each other.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1928: Keep your word on Rumania, Bulgaria and Serbia borders as agreed. Austria will not enter Rumania or Bulgaria. Tell me your fall orders for A SMY and A RUM so we both keep our Balkan holdings secure against England and any Russian moves.

In Fall 1928 I will leave BUD, VIE and TRI alone. F NTH and F HEL will stay out of Denmark and Holland. My campaign is against France; keep A WAR and A MOS away from my northern holdings and we can preserve this understanding.

My target remains France, not your southern centers. F ION and F TYS will stay out of Greece, Smyrna and the Aegean this fall. Please keep F SEV and A SYR away from my northern holdings while I finish the French campaign.

I am pressing your centers to reach the victory threshold. Keep A BEL out of HOL and tell me whether you will accept a settlement by yielding BEL and PAR; otherwise I will continue the attack. I am not directing my fleets against Italy or Turkey.

France to England, Fall 1928: Your fleets have held Marseille and Iberia while promising no moves on Brest. I am not conceding BEL, BRE, PAR, MUN or POR. Tell me plainly whether F MAO, F WES or F NTH will enter Gascony, Brest or Belgium this fall. If you refuse, I will defend every centre and look to other powers for help.

France to Italy: I hold A PAR, A MUN and F BRE this fall. A BUR can reach Marseille only if England's western fleets clearly leave Iberia, so I need to know your move first. Are you keeping F TUN and F NAP in place? Please tell me before any strike on Marseille or Spain.

France to Turkey: Thank you for keeping fleets off Greece and Smyrna. England is the common threat to Iberia and Tunis, and its fleets have grown too large. Will you press Austria in the Balkans this fall, or do you plan to shift forces west? Let us coordinate before England's fleets move.

Italy to England, Fall 1928: You lead by far and your fleets sit at TYS, TUS and near Venice. Italy needs concrete proof: withdraw F TUS from Tuscany and F TYS from the Tyrrhenian now, and I will keep F NAP and F TUN out of Spain and Marseille. Otherwise I must assume you are preparing to strike Naples.

Turkey to England, Fall 1928: Your fleets F ION and F TYS are the danger to Greece and Smyrna. Confirm in writing they stay out of the Aegean and Greece this autumn. You lead at 13 and I cannot let you reach 18 unchecked. Give me the French center you take first and I will judge your word by your moves.

Turkey to France, Fall 1928: England is near victory and its fleets sit in the Mediterranean. Hold Tunis-side and Iberian approaches with your fleets, and I will watch F ION and F TYS. Tell me your plan for Brest and Belgium so we can coordinate against England's northern push.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1928: England leads at 13 and must be stopped. Let us both block English advances, you in the north and I in the south. Keep A SER and A BUD out of Rumania and Bulgaria as agreed, and I will keep A RUM and F SEV off Galicia and Warsaw. Tell me your fall target so we avoid collision.

Austria to Turkey: Agreed that England must be checked. Austria holds BUD, VIE and TRI and will not enter Rumania or Bulgaria. I want to take Galicia and Warsaw-area centers myself, so keep A RUM and F SEV clear of Galicia. Send me your fall orders first so we avoid collisions, and let's coordinate against English fleets in the Aegean and Black Sea.

I will not send F TUS or F TYS against Naples, Rome, or Venice this fall, but I cannot withdraw them from the French campaign. Keep F NAP and F TUN out of Spain and Marseille, and we can avoid opening a second front.

F MAO will enter Brest, and F NTH will move against Belgium this fall. I will not send F WES into Gascony. You can still avoid further losses by yielding BEL and PAR; otherwise I will continue pressing your centers.

F HEL will hold and F NTH will move against Belgium, not Denmark or Holland. I will not move against Warsaw or Galicia this fall, and I will leave BUD, VIE, and TRI alone. Keep A WAR and A MOS away from my northern holdings.

F ION and F TYS will stay out of Greece, Smyrna, and the Aegean this fall. Belgium is my immediate target. Please keep F SEV and A SYR away from my northern holdings while I continue the French campaign.

France to Turkey: Agreed on watching the Mediterranean. France will keep F TUN and F NAP-side pressure off Greece and Smyrna. I will not move on Austria in the Balkans, so please keep pressing Trieste and Budapest with A SER and A BUL. If England's F ION or F TYS threaten Tunis or Greece, tell me at once and we will strike together.

France to England: No concession of BEL, BRE, PAR, MUN or POR. Your F MAO, F WES and F NTH have not been ruled out of Gascony, Brest or Belgium, so France will defend every centre. Withdraw those fleets in writing this fall and A BEL stays out of HOL. Otherwise expect French resistance.

Italy to France: I am holding F TUN and F NAP this fall and will not strike Marseille or move toward Spain without telling you first. England's F TYS and F TUS sit close to Italy, so I am watching them closely. If you move A BUR toward Marseille once England's western fleets leave Iberia, let us coordinate the timing in writing before any move.

Italy to Austria: Our Balkan plan stands. I have seen English F TYS and F TUS near Tuscany and Venice, not yet attacking. I will keep F NAP and F TUN ready, and will strike Marseille only if it opens and France has not moved first. Please keep A SER and F TRI off Venice, and tell me at once if England moves toward Greece.

Turkey to France: England is the threat, agreed. My fleets stay out of the western Mediterranean for now, but I will not commit to pressing Austria for you. Hold Tunis-side and Iberian approaches; I will watch F ION and F TYS and tell you at once if they move toward Greece or Smyrna. Share your Brest and Belgium plan first.

Turkey to Austria: Understood. A RUM and A BUL will not enter Galicia, Warsaw, Serbia or Trieste, and I expect the same from your A SER and A BUD toward Rumania and Bulgaria. My A SMY remains in the Aegean/Smyrna area against English fleets. Keep Russian moves in mind and tell me if your fall target changes.

Turkey to England: Your word is noted but your F ION and F TYS sit beside Greece and the Aegean. I need a firm answer: will you commit in writing not to move into Greece, Smyrna or the Aegean in Fall 1928 and Spring 1929? If so, I keep F SEV and A SYR off your northern holdings. Otherwise I will block you.

Austria to England, Spring 1929: You lead at 13 centers, which makes you the target of every power. Austria will not accept vague assurances again. Name the centers you will leave untouched this year and confirm F NTH and F HEL stay out of Denmark and Holland. Without written destinations, A WAR and A MOS stay on alert against your northern holdings.

I am continuing the campaign this spring: F MAO will press Brest, F NTH will press Belgium, and A RUH will move against Munich. Keep A BEL out of Holland and do not expect me to halt the advance. Will you pull back from Belgium or Munich rather than risk losing more centers?

My immediate attacks are on France, not Italy. I will not order F PIE against an Italian center this spring; please keep F NAP and F TUN out of Spain and Marseille while I finish the French campaign. Can we keep the western front contained?

My immediate target remains France. F ION and F TYS will stay out of Greece, Smyrna, and the Aegean this spring; please keep F SEV away from my northern holdings. I cannot promise to stop after France, but I am not opening a southern front this turn.

France to England: Your F MAO and F NTH are already moving on BRE and BEL, and yielding is not on the table. Spring 1929: state plainly whether F MAO, F WES or F NTH enter Brest or Belgium. If they do not, France will not move A BEL toward HOL and we can both stop bleeding. If they do, France defends every centre.

Italy to England, Spring 1929: Your fleets now sit at TYS, PIE and near Venice while you hold Marseille. You lead by a wide margin and Italy cannot accept that. Withdraw F PIE and F TYS from Italian waters and leave Marseille, and I will keep F NAP and F TUN out of Spain. Otherwise Italy will coordinate with France and Austria against your western holdings.

Turkey to England, Spring 1929: Your fleets F ION and F TYS are the threat I track. You lead with 13 centers, so I need concrete assurances. Confirm in writing that F ION, F TYS and F MAO will not enter Greece, Smyrna, the Aegean or Tunis this spring, and name which French center you take first. Silence will be read as hostility.

Turkey to Italy: England's F ION and F TYS threaten both of us, and it is clear England will not stop at France. Will you keep A VEN and F NAP out of Greece and the Balkans, and tell me your spring plan? I will keep A SMY and F SEV away from Venice, Rome and Naples. Let us coordinate to block England's Mediterranean fleets.

This spring F NTH is moving to Belgium and F HEL to Denmark; neither will enter Denmark from NTH or Holland. I will leave BUD, VIE, TRI, Warsaw and Galicia untouched this turn. Keep A WAR and A MOS away from my northern holdings while I press France.

I will not disguise my intentions: F MAO will press Brest and F NTH will press Belgium this spring. A RUH is directed against Munich. Keep A BEL out of Holland and you can avoid widening the conflict, but I will not halt the campaign.

F ION and F TYS will stay out of Greece, Smyrna and the Aegean this spring. F MAO will not enter Tunis. My first French target is Brest, with pressure also on Belgium and Munich. Please keep F SEV away from my northern holdings.

I will not order F PIE or F TYS against an Italian center this spring, and I will leave Marseille alone. My campaign remains focused on France. Keep F NAP and F TUN out of Spain and Marseille, and we can contain the western front.

France to England: Your F MAO into Brest and F NTH into Belgium are declared hostile acts, and France will defend BRE, BEL and MUN with every unit. A BEL stays put and will not enter Holland. I will not pull back from Belgium or Munich. Withdraw F MAO and F NTH and we can talk of stopping the bloodshed; otherwise expect full resistance.

Italy to Turkey: I agree to keep A VEN and F NAP out of Greece and the Balkans this spring. Italy is holding its line and will not move against your SMY or SEV forces. England's fleets are the shared danger, so please keep A SMY and F SEV away from Venice, Rome and Naples as you proposed, and let us each block England in the Mediterranean.

Italy to England: Your word means little while F PIE and F TYS sit in Italian waters. Withdraw F PIE from the Italian coast and F TYS from the Tyrrhenian, and I will keep F NAP and F TUN out of Spain and Marseille. Until then Italy reserves its options against your western fleets.

Turkey to England, Spring 1929: Your words are noted, but your fleets F ION and F TYS are the ones I watch, and you lead with 13 centers. I will not give written pledges that bind my fleets. Show me by your moves: keep F ION out of Greece and Smyrna, and F MAO away from Tunis. Name the French center you take first and I will judge you by what you do.

Austria to England, Fall 1929: Your F HEL to Denmark is a direct breach of our understanding, and F NTH is near Holland. Explain both now. Austria is a player, not a pawn. Confirm in writing that no English unit enters Galicia, Warsaw, or BUD/VIE/TRI this year, or A WAR and A MOS will strike your Baltic holdings.

Austria to Italy, Fall 1929: English F TUS and F TYS are near Venice and Tunis. Tell me if they are moving to Greece or Tunis before I commit A SER. I am holding SER and TRI off Venice as agreed. If Marseille opens, strike with F NAP or F TUN and share your orders first.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1929: England is the common threat. Send me your fall orders for A RUM and F SEV before I move. I will keep A BUD and A SER out of Rumania and Bulgaria. I am taking Galicia and Warsaw-area centers, so keep A RUM and F SEV clear of Galicia.

This fall my campaign remains against France. I will leave BUD, VIE, TRI, WAR and MOS untouched; F HEL will not move to DEN or HOL. Please keep A WAR and A MOS away from my northern holdings while I take French centres.

I am not opening a front against Italy this fall: F TUS and F TYS will not attack NAP, ROM or VEN, and I will leave MAR alone. Keep F NAP and F TUN out of Spain and Marseille, and we can avoid a western war while I finish France.

My immediate campaign remains against France. F ION and F TYS will stay out of Greece, Smyrna and the Aegean, and F MAO will stay out of Tunis. Please keep F SEV away from my northern holdings; what are your plans for this fall?

France to England: Your F MAO, F NTH and A RUH are attacking BRE, BEL and MUN. France will not yield a centre. Withdraw F MAO and F NTH from Brest and Belgium this fall in writing, and A RUH from Munich, and France will not move toward Holland. Otherwise every French unit defends.

France to Italy: England is pressing my northern and western centres with F MAO, F NTH and A RUH, and its fleets sit near Tunis and Marseille. I am defending BRE, BEL and MUN, so A PAR stays put. Please tell me whether F TYS or F TUS will move toward Tunis or Marseille this fall, so we can coordinate defence of the Mediterranean.

Italy to France: England leads with 13 centers and is the threat to us both. I propose a joint plan this fall: you keep A PAR and A BUR pressing Marseille and Spain while Italy holds F NAP and F TUN and watches F TYS. Tell me your exact fall orders so we avoid collisions, and I will not move against your centers.

Italy to Turkey: England is the shared danger. Please keep A SMY and F SEV away from Venice, Rome and Naples as agreed, and I will keep A VEN and F NAP out of Greece and the Balkans. If England's F ION or F TYS moves east, let us both signal that and block together.

Italy to Austria: Our Balkan plan stands, and I will keep F NAP and F TUN ready against England's western fleets. Please keep A SER and F TRI off Venice, and tell me at once if English F TYS or F TUS move toward Naples or Greece. I need your fall orders to coordinate.

Turkey to England, Fall 1929: Your fleets F ION and F TYS have stayed out of Greece, so far so good. Keep F ION out of Greece and Smyrna, and F MAO away from Tunis this fall. Brest is your stated target; take it and show me by your moves. Any move toward Tunis or the Aegean will be answered.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1929: Thank you for holding A VEN and F NAP out of Greece. England's F ION and F TYS remain the shared threat. If you press Tunis or Greece against England, I will keep A SMY and F SEV away from your Venice, Rome and Naples. Tell me whether F NAP stays put this fall.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1929: Our Balkan border holds: A RUM and A BUL stay out of Galicia, Warsaw, Serbia and Trieste. Your A ALB and A SER-area forces should stay out of Greece and Bulgaria. Tell me your fall orders for Russia's southern holdings, since A MOS and A STP are close to my northern interests.

Austria to Turkey: Agreed, A RUM and A BUL stay out of Galicia, Warsaw, Serbia and Trieste, and A BUD and A SER stay out of Rumania and Bulgaria. My Fall 1929 focus is Galicia and Warsaw-area centers, and A MOS and A STP will hold their Russian positions for now. Keep A RUM and F SEV clear of Galicia and share your southern orders before we move.

Austria to Italy: Understood. A SER and F TRI will not move on Venice. I will watch English F TUS and F TYS and share my orders before any move. If Marseille opens, F NAP or F TUN should strike, and please tell me your Adriatic and Ionian plans so we avoid crossing paths.

Austria to England: Your F HEL to Denmark breaches our understanding, and F NTH near Holland is a concern. Explain both now. A WAR and A MOS remain on alert. Confirm in writing that no English unit enters Galicia, Warsaw, or BUD, VIE, TRI this year, and that F HEL and F NTH stay out of Denmark and Holland. Words alone will not hold us.

F HEL has not entered Denmark; it remains in HEL, and I will keep it out of DEN and HOL this year. My campaign is against France, not Austria: no English unit will enter Galicia, Warsaw, BUD, VIE or TRI this year. Please keep A WAR and A MOS away from my Baltic holdings.

I will not withdraw F MAO, F NTH or A RUH while France refuses any settlement and continues to hold centres I need. I am pressing Brest, Belgium and Munich. If you are willing to discuss a specific withdrawal or transfer that ends the fighting, propose it; otherwise I expect you to defend.

I will keep F ION out of Greece and Smyrna, and F MAO out of Tunis this fall. Brest remains my first French target. My immediate campaign is still against France; keep F SEV away from my northern holdings and we can avoid opening another front.

France to Italy: Agreed on coordination. I will hold A PAR, keep A BUR and A MUN defending against England's A RUH, and F BRE defending Brittany. I will not move toward Spain or Marseille this fall. Please keep F NAP and F TUN in place and tell me at once if F TYS or F TUS heads for Tunis or Marseille. England is the shared threat; let us both press it.

Italy to Austria: Our plan stands. F NAP and F TUN stay ready against England's western fleets, and I will not move toward Greece or the Balkans. Keep SER and TRI off Venice. I will signal any move against English F TUS or F TYS before it happens, and share my fall orders once they are set.

Italy to France: England leads with 13 centers and is the real threat to both of us. I am holding F NAP and F TUN this fall and will watch F TYS and F TUS closely. I will not move against your centers. Please confirm your exact orders for A PAR and A BUR so we avoid collisions.

Italy to Turkey: Agreed. A VEN and F NAP stay out of Greece and the Balkans, and I ask that A SMY and F SEV stay away from Venice, Rome and Naples. If England's F ION or F TYS moves east, I will signal you immediately so we can block together.

Italy to England: Your fleets at TYS, TUS and near Venice still threaten Italian centers, so Italy will not accept assurances alone. Withdraw F TUS and F TYS from the Italian coast and stay out of Tunis, and I will keep F NAP and F TUN out of Spain and Marseille. Until then Italy keeps its options open.

Turkey to Austria: A RUM and F SEV will not enter Galicia or Warsaw this fall; my orders stay in Rumania and the Black Sea. Keep A BUD and A SER out of Bulgaria and Rumania as agreed. Watch Russia's southern holdings: A MOS and A STP are your concern, and I will not contest Moscow. Share your Galicia moves so we avoid collisions.

Austria to England, Spring 1930: You hold 15 centers and are one step from the win, so Austria will not stand idle. Your fleets F HEL and F NTH have been near Denmark and Holland. Name the centers you will leave untouched, and confirm no English unit enters Galicia, Warsaw, BUD, VIE or TRI. Without written destinations, A WAR and A MOS stay on alert against your northern holdings.

Austria to Turkey: Spring 1930 plan: A MOS and A STP stay on Russian positions, and I want Galicia and Warsaw-area centers. Keep A RUM and F SEV clear of Galicia. England's A SMY-area threat in the Aegean is growing, so share your southern orders before moving, and I will do the same for A BUD and A SER.

Austria to Italy: Spring 1930: A SER and F TRI stay off Venice. England holds 15 centers and must be checked, so if F TUS or F TYS move toward Naples or Tunis, tell me at once. Send your Spring orders first so we avoid collisions in the Adriatic and Ionian.

I am not opening a front against you this spring. Keep A WAR and A MOS away from my Baltic holdings, and I will keep English units out of Galicia, Warsaw, BUD, VIE and TRI. Can we maintain that separation?

I want to avoid widening the western war. Keep F NAP and F TUN out of Spain and Marseille this spring, and I will leave Italian centers alone. Are you willing to keep F NAP and F TUN out of my holdings?

My immediate focus remains the western front. I will keep F TUN out of the Aegean and away from your centers this spring; please keep F SEV away from my northern holdings. What are your plans for F SEV?

France to England: Spring 1930, I will defend BRE, BEL and MUN. Name a concrete withdrawal: F MAO and F NTH out of Brest and Belgium, A RUH out of Munich, all in writing. Without that, France keeps every unit on defence and your fleets near Iberia and Tunis will be watched closely.

France to Italy: Please confirm whether F TYS or F TUS is moving toward Tunis or Marseille this spring. I will hold A PAR and move A BUR only to defend Munich or Burgundy. England is the shared threat; if you hold F NAP and F TUN, I will not touch your centres.

France to Turkey: England now holds 15 centres and wins at 18, so Austria's collapse helps England most. Keep pressing Trieste and Budapest with A SER and A BUL, and tell me if F ION or F TYS threaten Greece or Smyrna. France will keep F TUN-side pressure off your Aegean centres.

Italy to England, Spring 1930: Your fleets at TYS and TUN are a clear threat to NAP and ROM. Italy holds F NAP and F TUN, not Spain. Please confirm in writing that F TYS will not move to Naples, Rome or Venice this spring, and that A VEN and F ADR stay untouched by you. Italy will keep its fleets out of Spain and Marseille.

Turkey to England, Spring 1930: England holds 15 centers and is the clear leader, so trust will not come cheap. Your fleets F ION and F TYS are not in Greece or Smyrna this turn, and I see F TUN sitting next to my sphere. Tell me plainly: will F TUN and F TYS stay out of Tunis, Greece and the Aegean while you fight France? Silence will be read as a move toward war.

Austria to England, Spring 1930: Your word has been broken before, so I will judge by written deeds. Name your Spring 1930 destinations for F HEL, F NTH, F DEN-area and A LON, A LVP. Confirm in writing that no English unit enters Galicia, Warsaw, BUD, VIE or TRI. Separation is possible only if your fleets stay out of Denmark and Holland this spring. A WAR and A MOS stay on alert until then.

F TUN will stay out of Tunis, Greece, and the Aegean this spring; F TYS will not move against Greece or Smyrna. My campaign remains against France. Keep F SEV away from my northern holdings, and tell me where it will go.
F TYS will not move to Naples, Rome, or Venice this spring, and I will leave A VEN and F ADR untouched. Keep F NAP and F TUN out of Spain and Marseille, and we can avoid widening the western war.
